task_17.title: Default pacman support for CachyOS
task_17.description: Conan 2.28.0 adds CachyOS to the set of operating system distributions that resolve to pacman as the default system package manager, allowing CachyOS users to rely on automatic package-manager selection.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recognizes CachyOS as a distribution whose default system package manager is pacman.

expectation.grounded: When Conan's system package manager selection logic receives the distribution identifier `cachyos`, it should resolve to `pacman` in the same default package-manager family as Arch, Manjaro, MSYS2, and EndeavourOS. Existing default mappings for other supported package managers and distributions should continue to behave as before.
expectation.conceptual: Users running Conan on CachyOS should get automatic pacman-based system package manager behavior without needing to manually configure or override the package manager.

constraints.grounded: The observable behavior change is limited to recognizing `cachyos` as a pacman-backed distribution. Existing default package-manager mappings, explicit package-manager configuration behavior, package installation commands, and non-CachyOS distribution handling must not change.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add CachyOS support without disrupting package-manager detection or system package installation behavior for existing platforms.

behavior: The distribution identifier `cachyos` is now included in the default pacman-compatible distribution set.
Automatic system package manager resolution selects `pacman` for CachyOS.
Previously supported pacman distributions such as Arch, Manjaro, MSYS2, and EndeavourOS continue to resolve to `pacman`.
Default selections for other package managers remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan resolves the default system package manager for a CachyOS environment, it should select `pacman`.
When system package management is invoked on CachyOS without a manual package-manager override, Conan should use the pacman-backed behavior.
When Conan resolves default system package managers for existing supported distributions, their selected package managers should remain unchanged.
When users provide explicit package-manager configuration, CachyOS recognition should not override that existing configuration behavior.

task_30.title: Document Command and Profiles APIs
task_30.description: Conan 2.28.0 improves the public API documentation and introspection surface for command execution and profile handling. The ConanAPI command and profiles sub-APIs are now explicitly described, CommandAPI.run documents how callers can invoke commands and consume their returned values, and ProfilesAPI documents its profile loading, listing, and detection behavior. Profile aggregation also no longer performs a standalone global configuration validation step before loading and composing profiles.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's public API clearly documents how to use the command and profile sub-APIs, while preserving the documented profile composition behavior and avoiding unrelated eager global configuration validation during profile loading.

expectation.grounded: ConanAPI.command should be exposed as a CommandAPI sub-API for calling other Conan commands, and ConanAPI.profiles should be exposed as a ProfilesAPI sub-API for processing and loading Conan profiles. CommandAPI and CommandAPI.run should be discoverable through public API documentation or introspection, with run accepting either a command string or a list of command arguments and returning the invoked command's result. ProfilesAPI should document that it can list, manage, load, aggregate, and detect profiles; its profile aggregation API should describe profiles, settings, options, conf, cwd, and context inputs, preserve the established priority order, and should not raise solely from the removed eager global configuration validation step.
expectation.conceptual: Users of the Conan Python API should be able to understand from the public API surface how to invoke Conan commands programmatically and how profiles are loaded, combined, listed, and detected. Loading a profile should focus on composing the requested profile data and command-line overrides, rather than failing early because of unrelated global configuration validation.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing CommandAPI.run command execution semantics for string and list inputs, including returning the underlying command result. Preserve ProfilesAPI profile aggregation precedence, where later profiles override earlier ones and explicit settings, options, and conf values override profile contents. Preserve ProfilesAPI.list returning an alphabetically ordered list of profile files from the default cache location, and keep ProfilesAPI.detect as a best-effort default profile detection API whose output is not guaranteed to be stable.
constraints.conceptual: The documentation improvements must not change how commands are executed or how profiles are composed, listed, or detected, except that profile loading should no longer be blocked by an eager validation step unrelated to the requested profile composition.

behavior: ConanAPI.command is documented and typed as the sub-API used to call other Conan commands.
ConanAPI.profiles is documented and typed as the sub-API used to process and load Conan profiles.
CommandAPI exposes documentation explaining that it can launch full Conan commands through the API to reuse command functionality.
CommandAPI.run exposes documentation that its command argument may be a string or a list of strings and that it returns whatever the invoked command returns.
ProfilesAPI exposes documentation stating that it is used to list, manage, and load Conan profiles.

The ProfilesAPI profile aggregation API documents its profile list, settings, options, conf, current working directory, and build-or-host context inputs, including pattern-qualified settings/options/conf and supported conf value/operation forms.
Profile aggregation no longer invokes eager global configuration validation before loading profile plugins, cache settings, and profile data.
ProfilesAPI.list documentation states that it returns an alphabetically ordered list of profile files in the default cache location.
ProfilesAPI.detect documentation states that detected profiles are best-effort defaults and may change over time under the same expectations as the profile detection command.
acceptance_criteria: When a user inspects ConanAPI, it should clearly expose command as the API for calling other commands and profiles as the API for processing and loading profiles.

When a user inspects CommandAPI.run, it should be clear that callers may pass either a command string or a list of command arguments and should handle the return value according to the invoked command.
When a user inspects ProfilesAPI profile aggregation, it should be clear how profiles, settings, options, conf, cwd, and build/host context inputs are interpreted.

When multiple profiles and explicit profile arguments are combined, later profiles should retain priority over earlier profiles and explicit settings/options/conf should retain priority over profile contents.
When profile aggregation is called in an environment where standalone global configuration validation would fail, it should not fail solely because of that eager validation step.
When profiles are listed through ProfilesAPI.list, the result should remain an alphabetically ordered list of profile files from the default cache location.
When a default profile is detected through ProfilesAPI.detect, callers should receive a best-effort detected Profile and should not assume the exact detected contents are stable across releases.

task_9.title: Filter HTML report diffs by extension
task_9.description: Conan 2.28.0 enhances the HTML output for report diffs so users can narrow visible file changes by file extension from the generated page. The update adds extension-specific controls, bulk extension toggles, and an extension-option search, while preserving the existing include/exclude path search and file-status filtering. It also addresses the reported HTML diff display issue where context lines were misaligned relative to changed lines.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users viewing `conan report diff ... -f=html` can filter the displayed file tree and diff content by file extension, including files without an extension, while preserving existing report-diff filters and aligned diff rendering.

expectation.grounded: The generated HTML for `conan report diff ... -f=html` should expose an Extensions section in the file-tree filtering controls. It should derive unique extension choices from the basenames of paths in the report data, sort extension choices, include a separate option for files with no extension when present, enable all extension choices by default, and allow each choice to be checked or unchecked. Changing extension selections should recompute the visible sidebar file entries and corresponding diff content together with the existing include path search, exclude path search, and moved/changed/new/old file controls. The UI should also provide controls to check all extensions, uncheck all extensions, and search within the extension-choice list.
expectation.conceptual: The HTML report diff should let users interactively narrow a large diff to relevant file types without regenerating the report. Extension filtering should feel additive to the existing search and status filters, and users should remain able to restore or clear extension selections from the page.

constraints.grounded: The extension filter must affect only presentation in the generated HTML report and must not change the underlying diff data. Extension matching should be based on the filename portion of each path, not directory names. Files whose basenames have no extension should remain filterable through a distinct no-extension option. Existing include/exclude text searches and moved/changed/new/old visibility controls must remain available and continue to participate in the final visibility calculation.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be an additive HTML viewing feature: it should help users hide or reveal groups of changed files without removing report content, weakening existing filters, or making extensionless files impossible to inspect.

behavior: On page initialization, the HTML report scans the report data paths and builds a unique extension filter model from each file basename.
All discovered extension choices are selected by default, so opening the report initially preserves the previous all-files-visible behavior subject to the existing filters.
When at least one changed file has no extension in its basename, the filter UI includes a distinct no-extension choice.
Unchecking an extension removes matching file entries from the sidebar and hides their associated diff content; rechecking it restores those entries when the other active filters also allow them.
The extension filter is evaluated together with the include path search, exclude path search, and file status controls when visible files are recomputed.
The extension controls include bulk actions for selecting all and clearing all extension choices.
The extension controls include a search field that filters the visible list of extension choices without directly changing which files are displayed.
The extension-choice list is presented as a bounded, scrollable control so reports with many file types remain usable.
Context lines in the HTML diff output should align consistently with adjacent diff lines rather than appearing offset by an extra character.
acceptance_criteria: Given a generated HTML report diff containing files with extensions, when the page loads, it should show extension filter choices for those file types and leave them selected by default.
Given a generated HTML report diff containing at least one file without an extension, when the page loads, it should provide a separate no-extension filter choice.
When a user unchecks a specific extension, files with that basename extension and their diff sections should be hidden from the report view.
When a user rechecks a previously hidden extension, matching files should reappear if they also satisfy the active text-search and file-status filters.
When a user activates the uncheck-all extension control, extension-based visibility should hide all extension groups; when the user activates check-all, all extension groups should be selected again.
When a user searches within the extension controls, the list of extension choices should narrow to matching choices without changing file visibility until selections are changed.
When include search, exclude search, or moved/changed/new/old filters are active, changing extension selections should combine with those filters rather than replacing them.
When the HTML diff renders unchanged context lines next to changed lines, the line content should appear consistently aligned.

task_32.title: Forward system package manager errors
task_32.description: Conan system package manager operations now expose actionable diagnostics from the underlying package manager or shell when an external command fails. Failures include more context such as the failing command, exit status, and captured output, while quiet command output remains hidden for successful or accepted outcomes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan system package manager operations surface underlying package manager failures, including missing tools and command execution errors, instead of reporting only a generic command failure.

expectation.grounded: System package manager helpers in conan.tools.system should raise ConanException when an invoked package manager command returns outside its accepted return codes, and that exception should identify the command, the numeric exit code, and any captured stderr or stdout made available during quiet execution. If no default system package manager can be detected and no tools.system.package_manager:tool configuration supplies one, or if the selected package manager is unavailable on PATH, Conan should fail early with an actionable error.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan cannot use the operating system package manager, users should immediately see why it failed, including relevant diagnostics from the external tool, without successful package-manager checks becoming noisier.

constraints.grounded: Accepted return-code handling for package manager commands must remain unchanged. Quiet executions must keep stdout and stderr suppressed when the command succeeds or returns an accepted status. Captured stderr and stdout should be included only when present and only for failing commands. Explicit package-manager configuration should continue to be honored.
constraints.conceptual: Improve failure visibility without changing which package-manager outcomes count as success, without adding noise to normal successful runs, and without overriding user configuration.

behavior: A system package manager command that exits with a non-accepted status now raises ConanException with the numeric exit code included in the failure information.
For quiet command executions, stderr captured from a failing external command is forwarded in the raised failure when available.
For quiet command executions, stdout captured from a failing external command is forwarded in the raised failure when available.
Captured quiet output remains hidden when the external command returns an accepted status.
Commands returning accepted status codes continue to return normally without raising.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Conan system package manager operation invokes an external command, when that command exits with a status outside the accepted return codes, then Conan should raise ConanException that identifies the failing command and its numeric exit code.
Given a failing quiet package-manager command writes to stderr, when Conan reports the failure, then the user-facing exception should include the captured stderr content.
Given a failing quiet package-manager command writes to stdout, when Conan reports the failure, then the user-facing exception should include the captured stdout content.
Given a quiet package-manager command returns an accepted status, when the operation completes, then Conan should not raise and should not surface the buffered stdout or stderr.

Given no supported system package manager can be detected and no package-manager tool is configured, when Conan needs a system package manager, then Conan should fail early with an actionable exception.
Given the selected package manager executable is not available on PATH, when Conan attempts to use it, then the resulting failure should expose the underlying command execution diagnostic.

task_15.title: Honor configured system package manager before default detection
task_15.description: Conan 2.28.0 changes system package manager tool resolution so an explicit profile or recipe configuration for the package manager tool is used directly, without first running default package manager detection. This prevents unnecessary platform or distribution probing when the user has already selected the tool, while preserving default detection when no configured tool is available.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that an explicit `tools.system.package_manager:tool` configuration override is honored immediately and does not trigger default system package manager detection.

expectation.grounded: When initializing Conan's system package manager helpers, read `tools.system.package_manager:tool` first and use that configured value as the active package manager tool when it is available. The fallback `get_default_tool()` detection path should only be evaluated when the configuration lookup does not provide a usable tool value.
expectation.conceptual: If a user configures which system package manager Conan should use, Conan should trust that choice and avoid auto-detecting another package manager. Automatic detection should remain available only as the fallback for users who did not configure a package manager tool.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the semantics of other system package manager configuration keys such as `tools.system.package_manager:sudo`, `tools.system.package_manager:sudo_askpass`, or `tools.system.package_manager:mode`. Do not remove or weaken default package manager detection when `tools.system.package_manager:tool` is unset or resolves to no active tool.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to avoiding unnecessary default detection when the package manager has already been selected. Existing behavior for unconfigured users and unrelated package manager options should remain stable.

behavior: A configured non-empty `tools.system.package_manager:tool` value becomes the active system package manager tool without evaluating the default detection method.
Default package manager detection still runs when no configured tool value is available.
Profile-provided package manager overrides no longer cause side effects from default package manager probing, such as distro detection work or detection-related warnings/errors.
System package manager options unrelated to tool selection continue to be read and applied independently.
acceptance_criteria: Given `tools.system.package_manager:tool` is configured with a package manager command, when a system package manager helper is initialized, then the configured command should be used as the active tool.

Given `tools.system.package_manager:tool` is configured with a package manager command, when the helper is initialized on an environment where default detection would otherwise probe the platform, then default detection should not be invoked.

Given `tools.system.package_manager:tool` is not configured, when a system package manager helper is initialized, then Conan should continue to detect the default package manager tool using the existing fallback behavior.
When `sudo`, `sudo_askpass`, or `mode` package manager settings are configured or omitted, their observable behavior should remain unchanged by this tool-selection change.

task_1.title: Allow Uploads to Disabled Remotes
task_1.description: Conan upload now provides an explicit opt-in flag that lets users upload to a target remote even when that remote is currently disabled. The default disabled-remote protection remains in place unless the new flag is supplied, and the upload flow continues to apply the existing package preparation, upload policy, metadata, and argument validation behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can intentionally run `conan upload` against a disabled remote by passing an explicit command-line option, while preserving the existing behavior that disabled remotes block uploads by default.

expectation.grounded: `conan upload` must accept a Boolean `--allow-disabled` option. When this option is present for a selected remote, the upload command should treat that remote as enabled for the current upload operation so the normal upload pipeline can proceed. Without `--allow-disabled`, attempts to upload to a disabled remote should continue to be rejected by the existing disabled-remote handling. `UploadAPI` should continue honoring `upload_policy='skip'`, metadata validation, package preparation, and SCM URL checks while loading recipes through the command's API helper loader.
expectation.conceptual: Uploading to a disabled remote should be possible only through an explicit user override. The override should allow the upload workflow to run normally for that invocation, without changing the default safety behavior for disabled remotes or altering unrelated upload rules.

constraints.grounded: The new option must be scoped to `conan upload` and must not change the existing behavior when the option is omitted. Existing validations for conflicting pattern/list inputs, package-query/list inputs, and invalid metadata combinations must remain unchanged. Existing upload behaviors such as dry-run, confirmation handling, package-list uploads, metadata uploads, upload-policy skipping, and local SCM URL restrictions must continue to apply.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should be an opt-in exception, not a broad change to remote management. Disabled remotes should remain protected by default, and enabling this upload path should not weaken other upload safeguards or unrelated command semantics.

behavior: `conan upload` exposes a new `--allow-disabled` command-line flag.
When `--allow-disabled` is provided, the selected remote is treated as not disabled for the current upload flow.
When `--allow-disabled` is not provided, uploading to a disabled remote continues to fail through the existing disabled-remote behavior.
The upload flow still performs the same argument validation for incompatible pattern, package-list, and package-query combinations.
The upload flow still validates metadata selection rules before package preparation.
Recipe loading used for upload-policy evaluation and package preparation is performed through the existing API helper loader, preserving upload policy and package preparation semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given a target remote that is disabled, when a user runs `conan upload` for that remote without `--allow-disabled`, it should be rejected because the remote is disabled.

Given a target remote that is disabled, when a user runs `conan upload` for that remote with `--allow-disabled`, it should proceed into the normal upload workflow instead of failing solely because the remote is disabled.
Given a target remote that is enabled, when a user runs `conan upload` with or without `--allow-disabled`, the command should follow the same normal upload behavior.
When `--allow-disabled` is used together with existing upload options such as confirmation, dry-run, package lists, or metadata selection, those options should retain their established semantics.
When an uploaded recipe declares an upload policy that skips binary upload, that policy should still be honored during the upload workflow.
When existing invalid argument combinations are supplied to `conan upload`, they should still be rejected regardless of whether `--allow-disabled` is present.

task_14.title: Add strict remote authentication mode
task_14.description: The remote authentication command now supports an optional strict mode so automation can fail when any matched remote cannot be authenticated, while preserving the previous permissive behavior by default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan remote auth` can be run in a strict mode that fails the command when authentication fails for any matched remote, while keeping the existing successful exit behavior for non-strict invocations.

expectation.grounded: `conan remote auth` accepts a `--strict` flag. When the flag is provided, the command must attempt authentication for the remotes matched by the requested name or pattern and raise a `ConanException` if at least one matched remote records an authentication error, causing a non-zero command result. The failure should identify which matched remote names failed. Without `--strict`, authentication errors for individual remotes remain part of the returned command result and do not by themselves make the command fail.
expectation.conceptual: Users can opt into CI-friendly remote authentication where any failed remote authentication makes the command fail. Users who do not opt in continue to get the legacy behavior where partial authentication failures are reported but do not make the command unsuccessful.

constraints.grounded: `--strict` must not change remote pattern matching, username selection, forced authentication behavior, or the per-remote success and error reporting produced by `conan remote auth`. Non-strict invocations must remain backward compatible and continue returning success even when some matched remotes report authentication errors.
constraints.conceptual: Strict mode should only affect the overall success or failure of the command after authentication has been attempted; it should not alter how remotes are selected, how credentials are requested, or how normal non-strict usage behaves.

behavior: `conan remote auth` exposes a new optional `--strict` flag.
When `--strict` is omitted, authentication failures for some matched remotes are collected and reported without making the command fail.
When `--strict` is supplied and every matched remote authenticates successfully, the command completes successfully and returns the normal per-remote authentication result.
When `--strict` is supplied and one or more matched remotes fail authentication, the command raises a `ConanException`, returns a non-zero result, and reports the names of the failed remotes.
Strict-mode failure evaluation happens after authentication has been attempted for the matched remotes, so successful remotes can still complete before the aggregate failure is reported.
acceptance_criteria: Given remotes that all authenticate successfully, when a user runs `conan remote auth` with `--strict`, it should complete successfully.
Given multiple matched remotes where at least one authentication fails, when a user runs `conan remote auth` with `--strict`, it should fail the command with a non-zero result.
Given multiple matched remotes where at least one authentication fails, when a user runs `conan remote auth` with `--strict`, it should identify the remote names that failed authentication.

Given multiple matched remotes where at least one authentication fails, when a user runs `conan remote auth` without `--strict`, it should preserve the previous behavior by completing successfully while reporting the per-remote authentication error.

Given existing options such as user selection or forced authentication, when `--strict` is used with them, it should preserve their existing authentication semantics and only change the aggregate failure outcome.

task_23.title: Remove deprecated system_tools profile support
task_23.description: Conan 2.28.0 removes the deprecated [system_tools] profile section. Profiles must declare platform tool requirements through the supported [platform_tool_requires] section; the old section is no longer accepted, mapped, or warned about as a deprecated alias.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan profiles no longer support the deprecated [system_tools] section and require users to declare platform tool requirements with [platform_tool_requires].

expectation.grounded: Profile parsing must stop accepting [system_tools], must not read entries from it, and must not use it as a fallback for [platform_tool_requires]. The [platform_tool_requires] section remains the supported way to provide platform tool requirements. A profile containing [system_tools] should be treated as an unsupported profile section by the existing profile validation behavior rather than being accepted with a deprecation warning.
expectation.conceptual: Deprecated profile configuration for system tools is fully removed. Users who need platform-level tool dependencies must use the current supported profile section, and obsolete profile syntax should fail instead of continuing through a compatibility path.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the behavior of other profile sections such as [tool_requires], [platform_requires], [platform_tool_requires], [settings], [options], [conf], [buildenv], [runenv], or [replace_requires]. Do not retain any compatibility behavior that converts [system_tools] entries into platform tool requirements or emits a deprecation warning for that section.
constraints.conceptual: Supported profile functionality should remain stable. The only intended compatibility removal is the old system tools profile section, and users should receive normal invalid-profile handling rather than a silent migration or legacy warning path.

behavior: The deprecated [system_tools] profile section is no longer an accepted profile section.
Entries under [system_tools] no longer contribute to platform tool requirements.
The supported [platform_tool_requires] section continues to define platform tool requirements.
The previous deprecation-warning path for [system_tools] is removed because the section is no longer accepted as deprecated syntax.
If both legacy and supported sections are present, only the supported [platform_tool_requires] section is relevant; the legacy section should still be handled as unsupported.
acceptance_criteria: Given a profile that declares platform tools using [platform_tool_requires], when the profile is loaded, then those platform tool requirements should be applied as before.
Given a profile that uses [system_tools], when the profile is loaded, then it should not be accepted as a valid platform tool requirement declaration.
When [system_tools] appears in a profile, it should not produce a deprecated-section warning as part of a compatibility flow; it should follow the normal unsupported-section behavior.
When a profile contains other supported sections, their existing parsing and behavior should remain unchanged.

When a recipe's declared tool requirement does not match a platform tool requirement declared with [platform_tool_requires], the existing resolution semantics for platform tool requirements should remain unchanged.

task_3.title: OR policy for required Conan version
task_3.description: Conan 2.28.0 changes version-gated policy evaluation so a project can opt into gated behavior either globally through core:policies or locally through a recipe required_conan_version declaration. Either source is sufficient to activate the newer policy behavior, while projects that do not opt in keep compatibility behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan treats a configured core:policies required_conan_version policy and a recipe-level required_conan_version declaration as independent opt-ins for version-gated behavior, so either one can activate the Conan 2.28 behavior gates.

expectation.grounded: When evaluating a version-gated policy for a ConanFile, Conan should consider both the global core:policies entry whose value starts with required_conan_version and the recipe required_conan_version declaration. If either version range opts past the gate's compatibility boundary, the gated behavior should be active. If neither source is present or neither source opts past the boundary, the gated behavior should remain inactive. Missing global configuration access on special dependency nodes should not raise during policy evaluation. The core:policies configuration help should document required_conan_version>=version as an opt-in policy family for 2.28 behavior gates, including transitive static library package ID handling, VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation based on the requirement run trait, and host-context consistent trait defaults when visible=False.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to opt into new Conan behavior either once in global configuration or directly in an individual recipe. A positive opt-in from either place should enable the new behavior, and older projects should keep legacy-compatible behavior when they have not opted in.

constraints.grounded: Do not require both core:policies and recipe required_conan_version to satisfy the same gate. Do not let a non-activating value in one source suppress an activating value in the other. Preserve inactive behavior when there is no required_conan_version policy and the recipe declaration is absent or does not opt past the gate boundary. Ignore unrelated core:policies entries when evaluating required_conan_version gates.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be additive and opt-in. Global and per-recipe policy declarations should cooperate instead of overriding each other, and existing configurations without the new opt-in should continue to behave as before.

behavior: core:policies recognizes required_conan_version-style entries as version-range policies for opt-in behavior gates.
For each gated behavior, Conan evaluates the global required_conan_version policy and the recipe required_conan_version declaration with OR semantics.
A gated behavior becomes active when either source declares a required Conan version range that opts past the gate's compatibility boundary.
If the global policy is absent or does not activate the gate, Conan still evaluates the recipe-level declaration.
If the recipe-level declaration is absent or does not activate the gate, Conan can still activate the gate from the global policy.
Dependency nodes without global configuration helper state do not fail global policy lookup.

core:policies documentation now describes deprecated compatibility policies and the required_conan_version>=version policy family, including the 2.28 gates for transitive static library package IDs, VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation based on run requirements, and host consistent=True behavior with visible=False.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe declares required_conan_version high enough for a Conan 2.28 gate and no global required_conan_version policy is configured, when Conan evaluates that gate, it should use the 2.28 gated behavior.
Given global core:policies contains required_conan_version>=2.28 and the recipe has no required_conan_version declaration, when Conan evaluates a 2.28 gate, it should use the 2.28 gated behavior.

Given one source opts into a 2.28 gate and the other source is absent or remains compatible with an older boundary, when Conan evaluates the gate, the opt-in source should be sufficient to activate the gated behavior.
Given neither global core:policies nor recipe required_conan_version opts into a 2.28 gate, when Conan evaluates the gate, it should keep the existing compatibility behavior.
When Conan evaluates policy gates for dependency nodes that lack global configuration helper access, it should continue without raising and fall back to recipe-level or inactive policy behavior.

When users inspect the built-in description for core:policies, it should explain required_conan_version-based opt-in policies and identify the Conan 2.28 behavior categories controlled by that policy.

task_16.title: Scoped output for conan export
task_16.description: The export command gains an experimental contextual output mode that reduces repeated recipe reference prefixes. Instead of prefixing every scoped log line with the same package reference, the command prints the scope once as a contextual header and indents the related messages beneath it, while preserving the existing output behavior outside that scoped mode.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan export` presents recipe-scoped output in a compact contextual form by printing the package reference once for a contiguous scoped block instead of repeating it on every output line.

expectation.grounded: `conan export` should enable scoped recipe output for its execution unless that behavior has been explicitly disabled. When `ConanOutput` writes a message with a non-empty scope while scoped recipe output is active, it should emit the scope as a standalone contextual header only when the scope changes or when scoped output resumes after unscoped output, then emit subsequent messages for that same scope as indented scoped content. When scoped recipe output is inactive or no scope is present, `ConanOutput` should keep the pre-existing output behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Export output should group messages by recipe context so users can identify the package reference once and read the related lines beneath it without repetitive prefixes. Output outside this export-specific contextual mode should continue to look and behave as before.

constraints.grounded: Scoped recipe output must be limited to the `conan export` command lifecycle and must not leak into later output after the command completes. Scope header tracking must reset when output becomes unscoped so a later scoped block is introduced clearly. Existing color and no-color output modes must continue to produce readable scoped and unscoped output.
constraints.conceptual: The compact formatting must improve readability without changing command results, package export semantics, or the formatting contract for unrelated commands and ordinary output.

behavior: `conan export` opts into the new contextual recipe output mode during command execution.
For active scoped recipe output, the first message for a scope is preceded by a single scope header.
Additional messages for the same active scope are printed as indented content rather than repeating the scope prefix.
When the active scope changes, the next scoped message introduces the new scope with its own header.
When output is created or reset without a scope, the remembered scoped header is cleared so future scoped output is introduced again.
When scoped recipe output is inactive, scoped messages retain the legacy per-line scope prefix behavior.
After `conan export` builds and returns its package list result, contextual recipe output mode is cleared.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan export` for a recipe whose reference appears in multiple output lines, the output should show that reference once as the contextual heading for the related block.

When multiple messages are emitted for the same recipe scope during export, only the first message in that contiguous scoped block should be preceded by the scope heading and later messages should appear as scoped content beneath it.
When export output moves from one recipe scope to another, the new scope should be announced before its scoped messages.
When unscoped output occurs between scoped blocks, the following scoped block should announce its scope again even if it uses the same scope value as before.
When scoped recipe output is not active, scoped output should continue using the previous per-line scoped format.
When `conan export` completes, later command output should not remain in the contextual recipe output mode because of the prior export invocation.

task_6.title: Colorize Conan config command output
task_6.description: Conan 2.28.0 adds terminal color styling to the human-readable output of config inspection commands so configuration names are easier to scan without changing the displayed configuration data.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config list` and `conan config show` make their human-readable output easier to read by visually distinguishing configuration names from their values.

expectation.grounded: For the text output used by `conan config list` and `conan config show`, emit each configuration key or name prefix, including its separator, with cyan CLI foreground styling, then emit the corresponding value using the normal output styling. The commands should continue to show the same keys, separators, values, and line structure as before.
expectation.conceptual: When users inspect Conan configuration from the terminal, configuration names should be highlighted while the actual configuration values remain unchanged and readable as ordinary text.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the configuration data returned or displayed by `conan config list` or `conan config show`. Do not colorize the value portion of each entry. Do not alter structured formatter behavior or the semantics of other config subcommands.
constraints.conceptual: This is a presentation-only enhancement. It must not affect configuration contents, command behavior, machine-readable output, or unrelated configuration workflows.

behavior: `conan config list` text output now applies cyan foreground styling to each configuration key/name prefix before the value.
`conan config show` text output now follows the same colorized key/name prefix presentation.
The value portion of each displayed configuration entry is emitted without the new cyan styling.
The visible textual content remains equivalent to the prior output apart from terminal color styling.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan config list` in text output mode on a color-capable terminal, each configuration name and its separator should be visually highlighted in cyan while its value remains normally styled.

When a user runs `conan config show` in text output mode on a color-capable terminal, each displayed configuration name and its separator should be visually highlighted in cyan while its value remains normally styled.
When the same configuration data is displayed before and after the upgrade, the entries, separators, values, and line breaks should remain unchanged except for the added color styling on names.
When a structured output format is requested, the command should preserve the existing data shape and should not introduce terminal color formatting into that structured output.

task_19.title: Expose bumped development version for TestPyPI publishing
task_19.description: The release automation for Conan wheel publishing now needs the development-version bump helper to report the exact version it generated, so TestPyPI publishing workflows can consume the timestamped package version after the version file is updated.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the development wheel publishing workflow can obtain the exact timestamped Conan development version produced during version bumping.

expectation.grounded: After `bump_dev()` updates Conan's `__version__` value from a development suffix to a timestamped development suffix, it should return the resulting version string. When the helper is executed as a standalone script, it should print that same resulting version to standard output for publishing automation to consume.
expectation.conceptual: Version bump automation should not only update the package version, but also expose the final generated version in a machine-readable way so publishing steps can use the same value.

constraints.grounded: The existing behavior of replacing a plain development suffix with a timestamped development suffix must be preserved. The reported value must be read from the updated Conan version metadata rather than inferred independently, and the change must not affect normal Conan runtime APIs or package-management behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The publishing fix should be limited to release automation and must not change how users interact with Conan during normal operation.

behavior: `bump_dev()` continues to mutate the Conan development version by appending a timestamp to the development suffix.
`bump_dev()` now returns the full updated version string after the mutation is complete.
Running the version bump helper as a script now emits the updated version to standard output.
The emitted version reflects the value stored in Conan's version metadata after the bump, allowing wheel publishing automation to use the exact generated package version.
acceptance_criteria: When the development version bump helper is run on a Conan development version, it should update the version to include a timestamped development suffix.
When `bump_dev()` completes successfully, it should provide the full updated version string to its caller.
When the helper is invoked as a standalone command, it should output the same updated version string that was written to Conan's version metadata.
Normal Conan runtime behavior should remain unchanged by this publishing automation fix.

task_21.title: Require explicit build-order ordering
task_21.description: Conan 2.28.0 makes the ordering mode for `conan graph build-order` explicit by requiring the `--order-by` option. The deprecated fallback behavior remains temporarily available through the new `core:policies` configuration list by enabling `deprecated_build_order_args`, with removal planned for Conan 2.32.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan graph build-order` no longer silently relies on the deprecated implicit ordering behavior, while still offering a temporary policy-controlled compatibility path for users who need the old behavior during migration.

expectation.grounded: `conan graph build-order` must require `--order-by` unless the `core:policies` configuration list contains `deprecated_build_order_args`. Without `--order-by` and without that policy, the command must fail with a `ConanException`. With the policy present, the command must continue using the legacy fallback and emit a deprecation warning. The `core:policies` configuration help must describe policy-based opt-in behavior, including `deprecated_build_order_args` as a temporary compatibility policy until Conan 2.32.
expectation.conceptual: Users must make build-order sorting behavior explicit by selecting an ordering mode. Projects that temporarily need the old implicit behavior can opt into it through configuration and should receive a clear deprecation signal.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the normal behavior of `conan graph build-order` when `--order-by` is provided. Do not allow missing `--order-by` to proceed unless `deprecated_build_order_args` is present in the list-valued `core:policies` configuration. Preserve the compatibility policy only as a deprecated path scheduled for removal in Conan 2.32.
constraints.conceptual: The change should make ambiguous command usage fail fast by default, while keeping an explicit, temporary migration path and avoiding regressions for users who already provide the required option.

behavior: `conan graph build-order` reads `core:policies` as a list and treats it as empty when unset.
When `--order-by` is omitted and `deprecated_build_order_args` is not enabled, `conan graph build-order` fails before continuing with build-order computation.
When `--order-by` is omitted and `deprecated_build_order_args` is enabled, `conan graph build-order` proceeds with the legacy fallback behavior and emits a deprecation warning.
When `--order-by` is provided, `conan graph build-order` proceeds through the existing graph build-order flow regardless of the compatibility policy.
Configuration-facing policy documentation identifies `deprecated_build_order_args` as the policy that temporarily restores omitted-`--order-by` behavior until Conan 2.32.
acceptance_criteria: Given no `deprecated_build_order_args` policy, when a user invokes `conan graph build-order` without `--order-by`, it should fail and tell the user that an ordering mode must be specified or temporarily restored through policy.

Given `core:policies` includes `deprecated_build_order_args`, when a user invokes `conan graph build-order` without `--order-by`, it should continue using the legacy behavior and warn that the behavior is deprecated and temporary.
When a user invokes `conan graph build-order` with `--order-by`, it should not require or depend on any compatibility policy to proceed.
When users inspect available policy configuration, they should be able to discover that `deprecated_build_order_args` controls the temporary compatibility behavior for omitted `--order-by` usage.

task_48.title: Opt-in package ID fix for transitive static libraries
task_48.description: Conan 2.28 adds an opt-in compatibility fix for package_id computation in static-library recipes so transitive non-header requirements, especially transitive static libraries, no longer unnecessarily affect the package ID when the recipe or global policy declares the new required Conan version behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that static-library package_id computation can opt into the Conan 2.28 behavior where transitive static library dependencies that do not expose headers stop contributing to the consuming package's package_id, while preserving legacy behavior for users who have not opted in.

expectation.grounded: When computing package_id for a recipe whose package_type is static-library, enable the corrected transitive static dependency behavior if either the recipe declares required_conan_version compatible with >=2.28 or global.conf defines core:policies with required_conan_version>=2.28. Under that enabled behavior, a non-header dependency carried with headers=False must not get a package_id_mode and therefore must not be added to the RequirementsInfo used for the package_id. Without the opt-in, retain the previous non_embed_mode behavior and emit a risk warning once per conanfile when such a headers=False dependency still affects package_id.
expectation.conceptual: Projects that explicitly opt into Conan 2.28 compatibility should get cleaner, more stable package IDs for static libraries by ignoring transitive library dependencies that do not affect the package's headers. Projects that do not opt in should continue to receive the old package IDs and a warning that the old behavior is suboptimal.

constraints.grounded: Do not override an explicitly configured require(package_id_mode=...) trait. Preserve existing build-context package_id handling, header-only package handling, header-only dependency embedding, and normal package_id participation for requirements that expose headers. Treat the recipe-level required_conan_version and global core:policies required_conan_version opt-in as alternatives; either one can enable the 2.28 behavior. Maintain backwards-compatible package_id results unless the 2.28 required-version policy is active.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be opt-in to avoid invalidating existing binary package IDs. Only dependencies that are irrelevant to the static library's public headers should be removed from the package identity calculation; explicitly requested dependency identity behavior and existing non-static behavior must remain stable.

behavior: A recipe-level required_conan_version declaration is recorded on the loaded conanfile so package_id computation can evaluate version-gated behavior.
A global core:policies entry using required_conan_version>=2.28 can enable the same behavior as the recipe-level opt-in.
During package_id computation, the transitive static-library fix is evaluated once for the current conanfile and passed into requirement package_id mode deduction.
For a static-library package, a header-only dependency continues to use the embedding package_id mode.
For a static-library package with a non-header dependency whose headers trait is true, the dependency continues to use the non-embedding package_id mode.
For a static-library package with a non-header dependency whose headers trait is false, the dependency keeps the legacy non-embedding package_id mode when the 2.28 opt-in is not active.
For a static-library package with a non-header dependency whose headers trait is false, the dependency is excluded from package_id requirements when the 2.28 opt-in is active.
When the legacy behavior is retained for a headers=False transitive dependency in a static-library package, Conan emits a risk warning at most once for the conanfile.
Explicit package_id_mode values on requirements continue to take precedence over the automatic static-library deduction.
acceptance_criteria: Given a static-library recipe with a transitive static dependency carried with headers=False, when the recipe declares required_conan_version compatible with >=2.28 and package_id is computed, then that transitive dependency should not contribute to the resulting package_id.

Given the same dependency graph, when global.conf enables core:policies with required_conan_version>=2.28 and the recipe itself does not opt in, then the transitive headers=False dependency should still be excluded from the resulting package_id.
Given both recipe-level and global policy declarations, when either declaration enables required_conan_version>=2.28, then the corrected transitive static package_id behavior should apply.

Given a static-library recipe with a transitive headers=False dependency and no >=2.28 opt-in, when package_id is computed, then the dependency should continue to affect package_id using the legacy mode and Conan should emit a single risk warning for that conanfile.
Given a requirement with an explicit package_id_mode, when package_id is computed, then the explicit mode should be honored regardless of the 2.28 transitive static opt-in.

Given a static-library recipe with a header-only dependency or a dependency that exposes headers, when package_id is computed, then that dependency should keep the existing package_id behavior rather than being excluded by the transitive static fix.
Given recipes that do not opt into the 2.28 required-version behavior, when package_id is computed, then previously generated package IDs should remain compatible with the legacy behavior.

task_42.title: Full-link same-package CMake components
task_42.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps so component dependencies declared within the same package are treated as full public links. This prevents generated CMake config targets from omitting an intra-package component link, especially for shared-library components, while preserving target naming and link-feature metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps generates complete public link relationships for components that depend on other components from the same Conan package.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps processes a cpp_info.components entry whose requires reference resolves to another component in the same package, the generated dependency entry for the required target must be marked as a full link regardless of whether the package or required component is PackageType.SHARED. The target name must continue to honor the cmake_target_name property when set, fall back to the package::component target form otherwise, and retain any cmake_link_feature property associated with the required component.
expectation.conceptual: A consumer linking to one exported CMake component should also receive the component dependencies that the package author declared inside the same package, including shared library component dependencies, so normal CMake usage resolves includes and symbols without extra manual links.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to same-package component requirements handled by CMakeConfigDeps. Dependency resolution for requirements from different packages must continue to follow the transitive requirement graph, and missing or skipped transitive package dependencies must not cause new failures. Existing custom target names and link features must remain observable in generated CMake configuration.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change how unrelated package dependencies are discovered or linked, and do not remove existing customization behavior for generated CMake targets.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps treats every same-package component requirement as a full link/PUBLIC dependency in the generated target configuration.
Shared-library components in the same package are no longer exempted from generated full-link relationships.
A same-package component dependency continues to resolve to the configured CMake target name when one is provided, otherwise to the package-qualified component target name.
The cmake_link_feature metadata for a required same-package component remains attached to the generated dependency relationship.
Dependencies that refer to components from other packages continue to be resolved through the transitive dependency graph, with skipped transitive dependencies ignored as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Conan package with multiple cpp_info components, when one component declares a requirement on another component from the same package and CMakeConfigDeps is generated, then the required component should appear as a full public link dependency of the requiring component.
When both the requiring component and required same-package component are shared-library components, CMakeConfigDeps should still emit a full link relationship for that dependency.
When a required same-package component has a custom CMake target name, generated CMake configuration should use that custom target for the link relationship.
When a required same-package component defines a CMake link feature, generated CMake configuration should preserve that feature on the dependency relationship.

When a component requirement points to a dependency from another package, CMakeConfigDeps should continue to use the existing transitive package dependency behavior rather than applying same-package component rules.

task_18.title: Add consistent requirement trait
task_18.description: Conan 2.28.0 adds a `consistent` requirement trait so private or hidden host requirements can still participate in dependency graph consistency checks. This lets `visible=False` requirements be used in diamond dependency graphs without losing version disambiguation, while still allowing explicit opt-out for hidden requirements that should remain independent.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan requirements support a `consistent` trait so `visible=False` host requirements can participate in version consistency and conflict resolution in diamond dependency graphs without having to become visible to downstream consumers.

expectation.grounded: Requirement declarations and `Requirement` objects must accept a `consistent` trait. Dependency conflict and version disambiguation decisions must be based on whether both competing requirement edges are consistent, rather than only on `visible` or `test` traits. With the Conan 2.28 required-version policy enabled, host-context non-build requirements must default to `consistent=True` even when `visible=False`; without that policy, the legacy default remains that visible and test requirements are consistent by default. A requirement with `visible=True` and `consistent=False` must be rejected with `ConanException`. Transitive requirements must preserve and combine consistency so a downstream edge is consistent only when the relevant incoming and outgoing edges are consistent.
expectation.conceptual: Users can keep dependencies hidden from consumers while still asking Conan to enforce a single consistent dependency version across the graph. Hidden host requirements should behave like normal consistency participants by default for recipes opting into Conan 2.28 behavior, while explicitly inconsistent hidden requirements remain isolated.

constraints.grounded: `consistent=False` must remain supported for `visible=False` requirements. `visible=True` and test requirements must remain consistent by default. Build-context requirements must not become consistent by default solely because of the Conan 2.28 host-context policy unless they are visible, test requirements, or explicitly marked consistent. Existing conflict behavior based on matching references and options must continue to apply. The `visible=False` trait must continue to hide requirements from downstream visibility even when `consistent=True`.
constraints.conceptual: The change must add graph consistency control without changing visibility semantics. Existing recipes that do not opt into the new Conan 2.28 policy should keep their previous default behavior unless they explicitly set the new trait.

behavior: A new `consistent` requirement trait controls whether a requirement participates in dependency graph consistency checks.

Conflict detection between two requirements now uses the `consistent` trait: if both sides are consistent, Conan must enforce compatible versions; if either side is not consistent, hidden requirements may remain independently resolved unless another conflict rule applies.
When the Conan 2.28 required-version policy is active, host-context non-build requirements default to `consistent=True`, including requirements declared with `visible=False`.
Without the Conan 2.28 required-version policy, the default consistency behavior remains limited to visible and test requirements unless `consistent` is explicitly set.
A visible requirement cannot be explicitly marked `consistent=False`; that combination raises a Conan exception.
Combining duplicate or aggregated requirements must retain consistency if any contributing requirement is consistent.
Copied and propagated requirements must preserve the consistency trait, and transitive consistency must require consistency on both the incoming requirement and the transitive requirement.
Build-require propagation must preserve the relevant `consistent` trait and must not force consistency or run behavior beyond the source requirement traits.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe opts into Conan 2.28 behavior and declares a host requirement with `visible=False` and no explicit `consistent` value, it should participate in version consistency checks as if `consistent=True`.

When a hidden consistent requirement and another consistent requirement in a diamond graph refer to the same dependency through compatible constraints, Conan should resolve the graph to a single consistent dependency version regardless of requirement declaration order.
When a hidden consistent requirement conflicts with another consistent requirement for the same dependency, Conan should report a version conflict instead of silently resolving independent versions.
When a hidden requirement is declared with `consistent=False`, it should not force version consistency with other requirements unless another existing conflict rule applies.
When a requirement is declared with both `visible=True` and `consistent=False`, Conan should reject the requirement with a Conan exception.
When a requirement remains `visible=False` but is `consistent=True`, it should stay hidden from downstream visibility while still affecting consistency checks.

When recipes do not opt into the Conan 2.28 required-version policy, requirements that are not visible or test requirements should keep the previous default consistency behavior unless `consistent` is explicitly provided.

task_10.title: Add compiler flags mapping plugin
task_10.description: Conan 2.28.0 adds an optional Python compiler flags plugin so consumers can translate, remove, or preserve dependency compiler and linker flags when compatible binaries built for another compiler or platform would otherwise expose unsuitable flags. The mapping is applied when dependency cpp_info flags are consumed, while existing behavior is preserved when no plugin is configured.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that consumers can customize compiler and linker flags exposed by dependencies, especially compatible binaries built under a different compiler or platform, by providing a flags_map plugin that adapts those flags to the consuming Conan context.

expectation.grounded: Provide an optional compiler flags plugin exposing flags_map and apply it when a consumer reads dependency cpp_info.cflags, cpp_info.cxxflags, cpp_info.sharedlinkflags, or cpp_info.exelinkflags, including the same fields on cpp_info components. The callable receives the consuming ConanFile context, the flag item name, and the current flag list; its returned list becomes the observable value for that access. If the plugin is absent or no consumer context is available, the original flag lists are returned unchanged. Stored package metadata and serialized cpp_info retain the original package_info values.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to configure Conan so dependency flags are adapted to the current consuming build environment at consumption time. Incompatible flags can be removed or translated before recipe code or build-system generators use them, while projects without custom configuration behave as before.

constraints.grounded: Limit mapping to cpp_info cflags, cxxflags, sharedlinkflags, and exelinkflags for root package data and components. Do not alter other cpp_info fields, dependency identity, package IDs, compatibility selection, recipe loading behavior, or package_info storage. Existing graph, local, workspace, editable, lockfile, remote, update, and python_requires workflows must continue to expose dependencies through the same public APIs.
constraints.conceptual: Only the consumed view of compiler and linker flags should change. Package creation, dependency resolution, and projects without an installed mapping plugin should remain stable and backward compatible.

behavior: When a compiler flags plugin is available, Conan associates its flags_map callable with conanfile helper state used while loading consumers and dependency graphs.
When a consumer accesses a dependency through self.dependencies and then reads cpp_info, Conan evaluates eligible flag fields using the consuming conanfile as context.
The mapping applies to cpp_info.cflags, cpp_info.cxxflags, cpp_info.sharedlinkflags, and cpp_info.exelinkflags.
The same mapping applies to component-level cpp_info flag fields as well as root package cpp_info flag fields.
The plugin receives the flag category being read and the current list of flags, allowing it to return translated, filtered, reordered, or unchanged flags.
If the plugin is not configured, or cpp_info is read without an associated consumer, the returned flag values are the original stored values.
Compatible binary selection still happens normally; the plugin changes the flags observed by the consumer after the compatible dependency has been resolved.
Serialized package metadata keeps the original package_info flag values rather than persisting consumer-specific mapped results.
acceptance_criteria: Given no compiler flags plugin is configured, when a consumer reads dependency cpp_info flag fields, then it should observe the same flag lists that were stored by the dependency.
Given a compiler flags plugin returns a modified list for cxxflags, when a consumer reads a dependency's cpp_info.cxxflags, then it should observe the modified list for that consumer.

Given a compiler flags plugin returns a modified list for cflags, sharedlinkflags, or exelinkflags, when those fields are read from dependency cpp_info, then the returned values should reflect the plugin result.
Given a dependency exposes component-level flag fields, when a consumer reads those component flags, then the same plugin mapping semantics should apply.

Given a compatible binary was built with settings different from the consuming profile, when the consumer reads dependency flags or uses generators that consume cpp_info, then the emitted flags should be mapped for the consumer context instead of blindly exposing incompatible producer flags.

Given a package is created or its cpp_info is serialized, then the stored flag metadata should remain the original values declared by the dependency and should not contain consumer-specific mapped results.

Given editable or workspace dependencies expose eligible cpp_info flags, when they are consumed through the dependency graph, then their observed flags should follow the same optional mapping behavior.

task_33.title: Deprecate build_requires in favor of tool_requires
task_33.description: Conan 2.28.0 begins steering recipe authors away from the legacy build_requires mechanism toward tool_requires with explicit traits. Existing build requirement declarations continue to work, but users receive deprecation warnings when they rely on the old recipe attribute or callable. The release note also defines the 2.28 policy/version boundary for VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation to respect a requirement's run trait.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users relying on the deprecated build_requires recipe API are warned to migrate to tool_requires with appropriate traits, without breaking existing build requirement declarations.

expectation.grounded: ConanFile processing must emit a deprecation-tagged warning when a recipe defines the legacy build_requires attribute and when a recipe calls self.build_requires(...) inside build_requirements(). The self.build_requires(...) callable must continue registering build requirements with the existing public arguments, including package_id_mode, visible, run, options, and override. Under the Conan 2.28 required-version or policy behavior described in the release note, VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation should respect each requirement's run trait.
expectation.conceptual: Recipes using the legacy build requirement mechanism should still work, but users should receive a clear migration signal toward the supported tool requirement model. Build environment executable paths should only be propagated when the dependency is intended to be runnable.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or change support for existing build_requires declarations or self.build_requires(...) calls. Do not alter the accepted arguments or registration semantics of self.build_requires(...). Do not warn merely because the build requirement wrapper exists; warn only when the legacy attribute is present or the legacy callable was actually used. Preserve tool_requires, test_requires, and normal requires behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be advisory and backward compatible for existing recipes, while avoiding false deprecation warnings for recipes that have already migrated.

behavior: Recipes with a non-empty legacy build_requires recipe attribute produce a deprecation-tagged warning during recipe initialization.
Invoking self.build_requires(...) inside build_requirements() records that the legacy API was used and produces a deprecation-tagged warning after build_requirements() runs.
Calling self.build_requires(...) still registers the build requirement with the same observable arguments and dependency semantics as before.
Recipes that do not declare or call build_requires do not receive the new deprecation warning solely from normal requirement initialization.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe that declares build_requires as recipe metadata, when Conan loads the recipe, it should emit a deprecation warning directing users to migrate to tool_requires.
Given a recipe that calls self.build_requires(...) in build_requirements(), when Conan runs configuration, it should emit a deprecation warning after the method is evaluated.

Given a recipe that calls self.build_requires(...) with supported arguments such as run, visible, options, or override, when dependencies are resolved, it should preserve the same build requirement registration behavior.
Given a recipe that uses tool_requires instead of build_requires, when Conan loads and configures the recipe, it should not emit the build_requires deprecation warning.

Given Conan 2.28 policy/version behavior for VirtualBuildEnv, when a requirement is not runnable according to its run trait, its bindirs should not be propagated as runnable build-environment entries.

task_28.title: Remove deprecated Node dependencies alias
task_28.description: The upgrade removes the deprecated graph node compatibility accessor that exposed a node's dependency edges through Node.dependencies. Consumers should rely on the canonical node.edges relationship data, while node initialization continues to provide editable output folder state.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the deprecated Node.dependencies graph API is no longer available after upgrading, and that dependency relationships are represented through the supported node edge API.

expectation.grounded: Node.dependencies must be removed as a compatibility property. Accessing it should no longer return Node.edges or emit a deprecation warning; callers that need graph dependency relationships should use Node.edges. New Node instances should continue to expose initialized editable output folder state with no editable folder selected by default.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should stop supporting the deprecated dependency alias and keep the supported graph relationship API as the source of truth. Existing graph node state unrelated to the deprecated alias should remain initialized normally.

constraints.grounded: Removing Node.dependencies must not change the behavior or contents of Node.edges, graph traversal through Node.subgraph(), or the default availability of other Node state such as edge storage, replacement tracking, skipped build-require tracking, and editable output folder state.
constraints.conceptual: Only the deprecated alias should disappear; supported graph behavior and normal node state should continue to work as before.

behavior: Node.dependencies is no longer defined as a property on graph nodes.
Accessing Node.dependencies no longer produces a deprecation warning and no longer returns the node's edge collection.
Node.edges remains the supported way to inspect dependency edges for a graph node.
Node instances initialize editable output folder state to an empty default value.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller attempts to read Node.dependencies on a graph node, it should behave as an unavailable attribute rather than returning dependency edges.
When a caller reads Node.edges on a graph node, it should still provide the node's dependency edge collection.
When graph traversal is performed from a node, it should continue to use the supported edge relationships and produce the same traversal semantics unrelated to the removed alias.
When a node is created, editable output folder state should be present with no editable folder selected by default.

task_45.title: Respect run trait in VirtualBuildEnv bindirs
task_45.description: Conan 2.28.0 introduces an opt-in fix for VirtualBuildEnv so automatically propagated build requirement bindirs respect the requirement run trait. Recipes or global configuration that opt into required_conan_version >=2.28 get the corrected behavior, while older policy modes keep the legacy propagation for compatibility. The release also deprecates build_requires in favor of tool_requires.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that VirtualBuildEnv no longer exposes executable bindirs from build requirements whose effective run trait is disabled when the Conan 2.28 policy is active, while preserving legacy behavior for projects that have not opted into the new policy and guiding users away from deprecated build_requires usage.

expectation.grounded: When a recipe declares required_conan_version compatible with >=2.28 or global.conf enables core:policies with required_conan_version>=2.28, VirtualBuildEnv must respect the effective Requirement.run value for build requirements and tool_requires. Automatic bindir propagation from cpp_info.bindir should occur for runnable requirements and should be suppressed for requirements with run=False. Explicit environment contributions such as buildenv_info and runenv_info remain applicable. Requirement propagation must preserve the upstream run trait and consistency semantics instead of forcing propagated requirements to be runnable. build_requires is deprecated as a recipe-facing mechanism in favor of tool_requires.
expectation.conceptual: Projects that opt into Conan 2.28 behavior should only receive executable paths from tools they actually declare as runnable. Tools marked as not runnable must not silently become available through the generated build environment, while existing projects that have not opted in keep their previous behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation for recipes and configurations that do not opt into required_conan_version>=2.28. Do not suppress explicit buildenv_info or runenv_info contributions. Do not remove support for existing build_requires recipes as part of this change; treat it as deprecated and direct users to tool_requires.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be backward compatible by default, limit the behavior change to the documented opt-in policy, and avoid blocking users who still rely on older recipe declarations.

behavior: The configuration policy description exposes required_conan_version>=2.28 as the gate for the VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation fix.
With the Conan 2.28 policy active, VirtualBuildEnv automatically propagates a build requirement's executable bindir only when the requirement is runnable.
With the Conan 2.28 policy active, a build requirement or tool requirement declared with run=False does not have its bindir automatically added to the generated build environment.
Without the Conan 2.28 policy active, VirtualBuildEnv preserves the legacy behavior of propagating build requirement bindirs regardless of the run trait.
Transitive requirement propagation preserves the originating run trait rather than converting propagated build requirements to run=True.
Propagated requirements retain the relevant consistency semantics from the originating requirement.
Users are steered from the deprecated build_requires declaration toward tool_requires.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe or global configuration that opts into required_conan_version>=2.28, when a build requirement is declared with run=False, then VirtualBuildEnv should not automatically place that requirement's bindir on the build environment PATH.

Given a recipe or global configuration that opts into required_conan_version>=2.28, when a build requirement is runnable, then VirtualBuildEnv should continue to make that requirement's executable bindir available through the build environment.
Given a project that has not opted into required_conan_version>=2.28, when VirtualBuildEnv is generated, then existing bindir propagation behavior should remain unchanged for compatibility.
When a build requirement provides explicit environment information, that explicit environment contribution should still be included even if automatic bindir propagation is skipped because run=False.
