When requirement information is propagated downstream, the observable run behavior should match the originating requirement instead of being forced to runnable.
When users encounter build_requires in the upgraded surface, it should be treated as deprecated in favor of tool_requires rather than as the preferred declaration mechanism.

task_12.title: Add certified and safe OS setting variants
task_12.description: The default settings model was expanded so users can model additional supported operating system configurations: VxWorks can now be expressed with a certified variant, Neutrino can now be expressed with a safe variant, and Neutrino 8.0 is recognized as a valid version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's built-in settings accept the newly supported VxWorks certified variant and Neutrino safe variant, while also recognizing Neutrino 8.0 as a valid Neutrino version.

expectation.grounded: The default settings schema must allow `os=VxWorks` with `os.version=7` and an optional `os.variant` value of `certified`; it must allow `os=Neutrino` with versions `6.4`, `6.5`, `6.6`, `7.0`, `7.1`, and `8.0`, and an optional `os.variant` value of `safe`. Existing configurations where these OS variants are unset must remain valid.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to describe certified VxWorks builds and safe Neutrino builds using standard Conan settings, and existing VxWorks and Neutrino profiles that do not specify a variant should continue to work.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or narrow any existing Neutrino versions, the existing VxWorks version, or existing no-variant behavior for Neutrino and VxWorks. The new variant values are scoped to their respective operating systems and should not imply additional variants for unrelated OS settings.
constraints.conceptual: The update should be additive and backward compatible: it should recognize the new OS configurations without invalidating established profiles or broadening unrelated settings.

behavior: Neutrino settings recognize version `8.0` in addition to previously accepted Neutrino versions.
Neutrino settings expose an optional variant dimension that accepts the `safe` variant.
VxWorks settings expose an optional variant dimension that accepts the `certified` variant.
Neutrino and VxWorks configurations without an explicit variant remain accepted.
The new variant values are accepted only as valid values for the corresponding operating system setting.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures `os=Neutrino` with `os.version=8.0`, Conan should treat the settings combination as valid.
When a user configures `os=Neutrino` with `os.variant=safe`, Conan should treat the variant as a valid Neutrino setting.
When a user configures `os=VxWorks` with `os.version=7` and `os.variant=certified`, Conan should treat the settings combination as valid.
When existing Neutrino or VxWorks profiles omit `os.variant`, they should continue to be accepted.
When unrelated operating systems are configured, they should not gain Neutrino or VxWorks-specific variant values as valid settings.

task_5.title: Add Conan policy controls for deprecated behavior
task_5.description: Conan 2.28.0 introduces a global core:policies configuration list for explicitly controlling selected behavior changes and temporary deprecated fallbacks. By default, graph build-order now requires an --order-by mode and empty version ranges are disabled; users can temporarily re-enable each legacy behavior with a dedicated policy until its announced removal. The policy list also provides a global required_conan_version gate for Conan-version-based behavior fixes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan exposes policy-based controls for deprecated behaviors while enforcing the new default semantics for graph build-order ordering and empty version ranges.

expectation.grounded: Register core:policies as a built-in global configuration list. Recognize deprecated_build_order_args to keep the legacy conan graph build-order behavior when --order-by is omitted, and deprecated_empty_version_range to keep accepting empty version range expressions. Without the corresponding policy, conan graph build-order without --order-by must raise ConanException, and graph output encountering a resolved [] version range must raise ConanException. With the corresponding policy, each case must proceed and emit a deprecated warning. A core:policies entry beginning with required_conan_version must take precedence over a recipe-level required_conan_version when evaluating Conan-version-gated behavior, including the 2.28 policy-gated fixes documented for transitive static library package IDs, VirtualBuildEnv bindir propagation based on the requirement run trait, and the host-context default for the consistent requirement trait when visible=False.
expectation.conceptual: Users should get stricter, clearer defaults in Conan 2.28 while still having an explicit, temporary compatibility switch for specific deprecated workflows. Global policy configuration should also let users opt into version-gated behavior consistently across recipes.

constraints.grounded: core:policies must be validated as global configuration and treated as a list. The deprecated_build_order_args and deprecated_empty_version_range policies must only affect their corresponding deprecated behavior and must not change executions that already provide --order-by or use supported version range syntax. Deprecated fallback behavior must remain visibly deprecated and tied to the announced Conan 2.32 removal horizon. The global required_conan_version policy must have priority over recipe-level required_conan_version for policy decisions.
constraints.conceptual: Compatibility should require explicit opt-in, be narrowly scoped, and remain temporary. Modern command usage and supported dependency declarations should continue to behave as before.

behavior: core:policies becomes a recognized global configuration key describing policy entries for deprecated behavior and Conan-version-gated behavior.

Global configuration validation occurs when Conan initializes or reinitializes its global configuration, so invalid policy configuration is rejected consistently before command-specific profile processing.
conan graph build-order now fails when --order-by is omitted unless core:policies contains deprecated_build_order_args.
When deprecated_build_order_args is present and --order-by is omitted, conan graph build-order continues with the legacy fallback and emits a deprecated warning.
A resolved empty version range expression represented as [] now causes graph output to fail unless core:policies contains deprecated_empty_version_range.

When deprecated_empty_version_range is present, empty version range usage continues to be accepted for compatibility and emits a deprecated warning that users should migrate to supported wildcard range syntax.
A required_conan_version policy entry in core:policies is evaluated before the recipe-level required_conan_version value for Conan-version-gated behavior decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Given core:policies does not include deprecated_build_order_args, when a user runs conan graph build-order without --order-by, it should fail with ConanException and indicate that an order mode is required.
Given core:policies includes deprecated_build_order_args, when a user runs conan graph build-order without --order-by, it should continue using the legacy behavior and emit a deprecated warning.

Given a dependency graph contains a resolved empty version range [], when core:policies does not include deprecated_empty_version_range, graph output should fail with ConanException and direct users toward supported range syntax.
Given a dependency graph contains a resolved empty version range [], when core:policies includes deprecated_empty_version_range, graph output should continue and emit a deprecated warning.

Given core:policies contains a required_conan_version policy, when Conan evaluates version-gated behavior for a recipe, the global policy should take precedence over the recipe-level required_conan_version.
Given users already specify --order-by for graph build-order and avoid empty version ranges, upgrading to Conan 2.28 should not require compatibility policies for those workflows.

task_24.title: Remove Deprecated Detect Compiler API
task_24.description: The upgrade removes the previously deprecated `detect_compiler` helper from the detect API. Consumers must rely on the supported compiler detection API instead of the deprecated compatibility wrapper.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the deprecated `detect_compiler` entry point is no longer available in the detect API, and that users obtain default compiler information through the supported replacement API.

expectation.grounded: `conan.internal.api.detect.detect_api.detect_compiler` must be removed as an importable or callable API. Code that imports or accesses it should receive the standard Python unavailable-symbol behavior for that access pattern, while `detect_default_compiler()` remains the supported API for detecting the default compiler.
expectation.conceptual: The deprecated compiler-detection shortcut should no longer be part of the library surface. Users should use the current compiler detection API and adapt to its supported return contract.

constraints.grounded: Removing `detect_compiler` must not change the behavior of existing supported detect helpers such as `detect_default_compiler()`, `detect_gcc_compiler()`, or `detect_intel_compiler()`. The deprecated wrapper's prior two-value return contract and deprecation warning are not preserved.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should remove only the obsolete compatibility path while keeping supported compiler detection behavior stable.

behavior: `detect_compiler` is no longer defined by the detect API module.
Importing `detect_compiler` directly from the detect API fails because the symbol is absent.
Looking up `detect_compiler` as an attribute of the detect API module fails because the symbol is absent.
Calling `detect_default_compiler()` remains the way to detect the default compiler and returns the supported compiler detection result instead of the removed wrapper's shortened result.
No deprecation warning is emitted for `detect_compiler` because the deprecated function is no longer present.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer attempts to import `detect_compiler` from the detect API, it should fail with the normal unavailable import signal.
When a consumer attempts to access `detect_compiler` on the detect API module, it should fail with the normal missing attribute signal.
When a consumer uses `detect_default_compiler()` for default compiler detection, it should continue to provide compiler detection information through the supported API.
When supported compiler-specific detection helpers are used, their observable detection behavior should remain unchanged by the removal of the deprecated wrapper.
When upgrading from 2.27.1 to 2.28.0, code that still depends on `detect_compiler` should be treated as requiring migration rather than receiving a compatibility warning.

task_39.title: Support Xcode 26.4 and Apple Clang 21
task_39.description: Conan 2.28.0 expands its built-in Apple platform settings so projects using Xcode 26.4 and Apple Clang 21 can be represented with valid settings. The update adds the new Apple OS and SDK version values where applicable and recognizes Apple Clang 21 version identifiers, preventing valid modern Apple toolchains from being rejected during settings validation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan accepts and models Apple toolchains from Xcode 26.4, including Apple Clang 21, across the supported Apple platform settings.

expectation.grounded: The default Conan settings must accept Apple Clang compiler versions 21 and 21.0. The Apple platform version settings must accept OS version 26.4 for iOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, and Macos. The Apple mobile, wearable, TV, and vision platform SDK version settings must accept SDK version 26.4 for iOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS.
expectation.conceptual: Users working with current Apple developer tools should be able to configure Conan profiles for Xcode 26.4 without encountering unsupported compiler, OS version, or SDK version validation failures for the newly supported values.

constraints.grounded: Existing supported Apple OS versions, SDK versions, SDK names, Apple Clang versions, libcxx options, C++ standard values, and C standard values must remain accepted. The change must only broaden the accepted version matrix for the newly supported Xcode 26.4 and Apple Clang 21 values and must not remove or rename prior settings.
constraints.conceptual: The update should preserve compatibility with existing Apple profiles while allowing users to adopt the newer Xcode release and compiler version.

behavior: Profiles or settings that specify compiler apple-clang with version 21 are now valid.
Profiles or settings that specify compiler apple-clang with version 21.0 are now valid.
Apple platform settings that specify OS version 26.4 are now valid for iOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, and Macos.
Apple SDK version 26.4 is now valid for iOS SDKs, watchOS SDKs, tvOS SDKs, and visionOS SDKs.
Older Apple platform, SDK, and Apple Clang version values continue to be recognized as before.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile uses Apple Clang version 21, it should pass settings validation.
When a Conan profile uses Apple Clang version 21.0, it should pass settings validation.
When a Conan profile targets iOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, or Macos with OS version 26.4, it should pass settings validation.
When a Conan profile targets iOS, watchOS, tvOS, or visionOS with SDK version 26.4, it should pass settings validation.
When an existing profile uses previously supported Apple OS, SDK, or Apple Clang version values, it should continue to behave as it did before the update.

task_41.title: Preserve run trait for build requirements
task_41.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes dependency graph trait propagation for build and tool requirements. Upstream shared-library dependencies reached through a build requirement now inherit the originating requirement's run trait instead of always being treated as runnable, preventing false runtime propagation and avoidable version conflicts for requirements declared with run=false.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that build or tool requirements declared with run=false do not cause their upstream shared-library dependencies to be treated as runnable runtime dependencies in downstream dependency graphs.

expectation.grounded: When Conan propagates a transitive Requirement through a build/tool requirement to an upstream shared dependency, the propagated requirement must retain build=true, headers=false, libs=false, direct=false, and must set run according to the originating build/tool requirement's run trait. The propagated relationship must also preserve the originating requirement's visibility and consistency semantics so dependency conflict behavior follows the same scope as the original requirement.
expectation.conceptual: A dependency used only as a non-runnable build tool should not make that tool's own shared-library dependencies behave like runtime dependencies of the consumer. Runtime propagation should occur only when the originating build requirement is actually runnable.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing propagation for build/tool requirements with run=true or for dependencies that already require runtime propagation. Do not expose headers or libraries from upstream build dependencies to consumers, and do not make propagated upstream dependencies direct requirements.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve existing dependency graph behavior except for removing the incorrect runtime marking from non-runnable build dependency chains. Build-only dependencies should remain isolated from normal consumer link and include semantics.

behavior: A shared-library dependency upstream of a build/tool requirement declared with run=false is propagated as a build dependency with run=false.
A shared-library dependency upstream of a build/tool requirement declared with run=true continues to be propagated with runnable semantics.
Propagated upstream build dependencies remain non-header, non-library, and indirect relationships in the consumer graph.
Version consistency and visibility handling for propagated upstream build dependencies follows the originating build/tool requirement instead of introducing stricter runtime-scoped conflicts.
Dependency graph resolution no longer reports conflicts solely because multiple non-runnable build/tool requirements depend on different versions of the same shared library.
acceptance_criteria: Given a consumer with a build/tool requirement declared run=false, when that tool depends on a shared library, then the shared library should appear only as a non-runnable build dependency in the resolved graph.

Given multiple build/tool requirements declared run=false that depend on different versions of an upstream shared library, when resolving the consumer graph, then those upstream shared-library dependencies should not be promoted to runtime dependencies and should not conflict solely due to that promotion.
Given a build/tool requirement declared run=true, when its upstream shared-library dependencies are propagated, then their runnable behavior should remain enabled.
When upstream dependencies are propagated through a build/tool requirement, they should not expose headers or libraries to the downstream consumer and should remain indirect relationships.
When visibility or consistency rules apply to the originating build/tool requirement, propagated upstream dependencies should follow the same scope for conflict detection.

task_13.title: Support recipe-name patterns in --update
task_13.description: Conan 2.28.0 extends the -u/--update option so users can target updates with shell-style patterns over recipe names instead of only exact recipe names. Existing no-argument update-all behavior and version range update semantics remain unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Allow users to selectively update cached recipes by passing recipe-name patterns to -u/--update, while preserving existing exact-name and update-all behavior.

expectation.grounded: -u/--update accepts optional values as recipe-name patterns. When update selection is evaluated for a recipe reference, each supplied value is matched against reference.name using shell-style wildcard semantics; any matching pattern enables update for that reference. A bare --update continues to behave as an update-all request. Boolean update inputs continue to return their boolean value.
expectation.conceptual: Users can update all recipes whose names match a simple wildcard pattern, such as a shared prefix, without listing each recipe. The matching scope is recipe names only, not complete references.

constraints.grounded: Pattern matching must not consider recipe version, user/channel, revision, package identifiers, or the consumer placeholder. Values that include version or revision syntax should not accidentally match by those parts. Existing behavior for --update without a value, exact recipe-name values, disabled updates, and version-range resolution remains compatible.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should broaden selective update targeting without changing what versions are chosen, without changing update-all behavior, and without treating full reference strings as valid pattern targets.

behavior: Supplying --update without a value enables update checks for every recipe reference in the graph.
Supplying --update <name> continues to enable update checks only for references whose recipe name exactly matches <name>.
Supplying --update <pattern> enables update checks for references whose recipe name matches the shell-style wildcard pattern.
Multiple --update values are cumulative; a reference is eligible if its recipe name matches any supplied pattern.
Pattern evaluation is performed against the recipe name only, so patterns or values that rely on versions, revisions, or slash-separated full references do not match by those fields.
The consumer pattern marker has no effect on update selection.
Version range resolution still updates to the latest satisfying version and latest revision according to the preexisting --update semantics.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a command with bare --update, it should consider newer versions or revisions for all recipe references in the dependency graph.
When a user supplies --update liba, only recipe references named liba should be eligible for update.
When a user supplies a wildcard name pattern such as --update lib*, every recipe whose name matches that pattern should be eligible for update.
When a user supplies a value that includes a version or revision, it should not match a recipe merely because that version or revision is present in the full reference.
When a user supplies multiple --update values, a recipe should be eligible if any one value matches its recipe name.
When dependency resolution uses a version range with --update, the selected version should remain the latest version satisfying the range, with the latest revision for that resolved version.

task_11.title: Allow install_strip to target build systems
task_11.description: The tools.build:install_strip configuration now supports both the existing boolean form and a list form that enables install-time binary stripping only for selected build integrations. This lets users opt in to stripping for CMake, Meson, or Autotools individually instead of applying the setting to every supported backend.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can configure install-time binary stripping for only the build system integrations that support or require it, while preserving the previous all-or-nothing boolean behavior.

expectation.grounded: tools.build:install_strip must accept either a boolean or a list. A boolean value applies to CMake.install(), Meson.install(), and Autotools.install() as before. A list value applies stripping only to the named backend entries: cmake enables CMake install stripping, meson enables Meson install stripping, and autotools enables the Autotools install-strip target. Invalid non-boolean, non-list values should continue to be rejected through the configuration type validation behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users can choose whether binary stripping during install applies globally or only to selected build-system backends. Existing boolean configuration remains valid, and unsupported configuration shapes are not silently accepted.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable install command semantics for tools.build:install_strip=True, tools.build:install_strip=False, or an unset tools.build:install_strip value. For list values, each integration must ignore list entries for other supported backends. CMake must continue to honor its existing deprecated install-strip configuration path in addition to the new tools.build:install_strip behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The feature must be backward compatible for existing users and must avoid forcing stripping in build systems that were not selected by the user.

behavior: The built-in configuration metadata describes tools.build:install_strip as accepting either a boolean or a list of supported backend names.
When tools.build:install_strip is a boolean true value, CMake, Meson, and Autotools installs request stripped binaries as they did previously.
When tools.build:install_strip is a boolean false value or is unset, CMake, Meson, and Autotools installs do not request stripping from this configuration.
When tools.build:install_strip is a list containing cmake, CMake install requests stripping; when the list omits cmake, CMake install does not request stripping from this configuration.
When tools.build:install_strip is a list containing meson, Meson install requests stripping; when the list omits meson, Meson install does not request stripping.
When tools.build:install_strip is a list containing autotools, Autotools install uses the stripped install target; when the list omits autotools, Autotools install uses the normal install target.
When tools.build:install_strip is neither a boolean nor a list, the configuration remains invalid instead of being interpreted as a backend selector.
acceptance_criteria: Given tools.build:install_strip is true, when installing with CMake, Meson, or Autotools, then the install operation should request stripped binaries for that backend.
Given tools.build:install_strip is false or unset, when installing with CMake, Meson, or Autotools, then the install operation should not request stripping from this configuration.

Given tools.build:install_strip lists only cmake, when installing with CMake then stripping should be requested, and when installing with Meson or Autotools then stripping should not be requested by this setting.

Given tools.build:install_strip lists only meson, when installing with Meson then stripping should be requested, and when installing with CMake or Autotools then stripping should not be requested by this setting.

Given tools.build:install_strip lists only autotools, when installing with Autotools then the stripped install target should be used, and when installing with CMake or Meson then stripping should not be requested by this setting.

Given tools.build:install_strip contains multiple supported backend names, when installing with any listed backend then stripping should be requested for that backend, and unlisted backends should remain unaffected.

Given tools.build:install_strip is provided in an unsupported value shape, when an affected install integration reads it, then configuration validation should reject the value rather than enabling stripping implicitly.

task_22.title: Disallow empty version ranges by default
task_22.description: Conan 2.28.0 changes empty version range handling from a deprecated warning path to a default error. Users who still need the old behavior can temporarily opt in through the core:policies configuration using deprecated_empty_version_range, which preserves compatibility with a deprecation warning until Conan 2.32.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that package requirements using an empty version range are rejected by default, while providing a documented temporary compatibility policy for users who still rely on the deprecated behavior.

expectation.grounded: When Conan resolves a graph containing a requirement whose version range is the empty range expression [], graph output should raise ConanException by default and direct users toward the supported wildcard version range syntax. If core:policies is configured as a list containing deprecated_empty_version_range, the same empty range should remain accepted temporarily and emit a deprecated warning instead of failing.
expectation.conceptual: Empty version ranges should no longer be accepted silently or treated as ordinary deprecated usage. They should fail by default, with an explicit opt-in compatibility switch that keeps existing projects working temporarily while warning users to migrate.

constraints.grounded: The deprecated_empty_version_range policy must be read from the core:policies list configuration, and its fallback behavior is only a temporary compatibility path scheduled for removal in Conan 2.32. Supported version range expressions, including the wildcard form, must continue to work without requiring this policy. Other policy entries in core:policies must remain independent and must not enable empty version range support unless deprecated_empty_version_range is present.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be narrow: valid version range usage must keep working, deprecated compatibility must require explicit user choice, and the compatibility mode must clearly remain temporary.

behavior: A resolved dependency graph containing an empty version range expression now fails by default instead of only producing a deprecation warning.
The failure is surfaced as a ConanException during graph output for resolved version ranges.
Configuring core:policies with deprecated_empty_version_range restores the previous acceptance of empty version ranges for compatibility.
When the compatibility policy is active, Conan emits a deprecated warning rather than raising an error.
The policy metadata describes deprecated_empty_version_range as a temporary behavior-preserving policy planned for removal in Conan 2.32.
The policy metadata also exposes core:policies as a list of opt-in behavior controls for deprecated or version-gated Conan behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package graph with a requirement using [], when Conan prints or reports resolved version ranges without deprecated_empty_version_range configured, it should fail with a ConanException.

Given the same graph and core:policies containing deprecated_empty_version_range, when Conan prints or reports resolved version ranges, it should complete the deprecated empty range path and emit a deprecated warning.
When a user uses a supported wildcard range instead of an empty range, Conan should not require deprecated_empty_version_range and should not fail because of empty range handling.
When core:policies contains unrelated policy names but not deprecated_empty_version_range, empty version range usage should still be rejected by default.
When Conan describes available policies, deprecated_empty_version_range should be presented as a temporary compatibility option with a removal target of Conan 2.32.

task_20.title: Fix workspace lockfile handling
task_20.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes lockfile handling for workspace install and build commands so they consistently use a workspace-level lockfile when one is explicitly provided or found at the workspace root, while ignoring package-local lockfiles that could otherwise affect individual workspace package operations. The fix also prevents failures when combining an explicit lockfile with partial lockfile mode.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan workspace install` and `conan workspace build` consistently honor a single workspace-level lockfile, support partial lockfile mode without crashing, and ignore lockfiles located inside individual workspace package folders unless the user explicitly selects such a lockfile.

expectation.grounded: For `conan workspace install` and `conan workspace build`, resolve lockfile input in the workspace root context. When `--lockfile` is provided, use that lockfile consistently for all package operations, including when `--lockfile-partial` is also provided. When no lockfile is provided but a default `conan.lock` exists at the workspace root, use it as the global workspace lockfile. When no global lockfile is available, or lockfile usage is explicitly disabled with an empty `--lockfile` value, do not allow package-local `conan.lock` files to be discovered during the workspace package operations. Apply normal lockfile configuration validation to any resolved lockfile.
expectation.conceptual: Workspace install and build should have deterministic, workspace-wide lockfile behavior: an explicit or root-level lockfile applies uniformly to the whole workspace, partial mode works with that lockfile, and unrelated lockfiles inside package directories do not change the dependency graph.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public command surface of `conan workspace install` or `conan workspace build` beyond the corrected lockfile behavior. Preserve existing profile, remote, build, and partial-lockfile options. Do not fall back to package-local lockfiles during workspace operations when the user did not explicitly request them.
constraints.conceptual: Keep workspace operations predictable and backward compatible except for removing the unintended influence of local package lockfiles and the crash around explicit partial lockfile usage.

behavior: `conan workspace install` and `conan workspace build` resolve default lockfiles from the workspace root rather than from individual package folders.
An explicitly supplied `--lockfile` is propagated as the single lockfile choice for every package operation performed by the workspace command.
Combining an explicit `--lockfile` with `--lockfile-partial` no longer crashes during workspace install or build.
A root-level default `conan.lock` is automatically used as the global workspace lockfile when no explicit lockfile argument is provided.
If no workspace-level lockfile is selected, workspace package operations run with lockfile discovery disabled so package-local lockfiles are ignored.
An empty `--lockfile` value continues to mean that lockfile usage is disabled for the workspace command.
Resolved lockfiles are checked with the standard lockfile configuration validation before the workspace operation proceeds.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace command with `--lockfile` and `--lockfile-partial`, when `conan workspace install` or `conan workspace build` runs, then it should complete using the supplied lockfile rather than failing during lockfile handling.
Given a `conan.lock` at the workspace root and no explicit `--lockfile`, when a workspace install or build runs, then it should use that root lockfile consistently for all packages in the workspace.
Given `conan.lock` files inside workspace package folders but no selected workspace-level lockfile, when a workspace install or build runs, then those package-local lockfiles should not be used.
Given an empty `--lockfile` value, when a workspace install or build runs, then lockfile usage should remain disabled for the workspace operation.
Given a selected lockfile with invalid configuration, when a workspace install or build starts, then the command should surface the normal lockfile configuration validation failure.

task_34.title: Inline XcodeDeps transitive metadata
task_34.description: XcodeDeps should avoid recursive xcconfig include chains by generating xcconfig outputs only for direct dependencies and by inlining the required transitive CppInfo metadata into each direct package or component's conditional props file. This keeps Xcode build settings complete while preventing recursion-depth crashes in deep component dependency graphs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that XcodeDeps generated xcconfig files for direct dependencies contain all required transitive dependency settings without relying on inter-package include chains, so projects with deep or component-heavy dependency graphs do not crash Xcode.

expectation.grounded: XcodeDeps must generate package and component xcconfig outputs only for direct, non-build, non-skipped dependencies. For each generated root package or component conditional props file, it must merge the current CppInfo with recursively required CppInfo from internal component requirements and external package/component requirements, covering build metadata such as include directories, libraries, frameworks, defines, and flags. External requirements to packages without components resolve to the package root CppInfo; requirements to a whole componentized package resolve to all of its components; requirements to a specific component resolve only that component and its own transitive requirements. Generated package/component entrypoint xcconfigs must not include other packages' transitive xcconfig entrypoints.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers using XcodeDeps should receive self-contained direct dependency configuration files: all build settings needed from reachable transitive dependencies are already present, while unrelated components and skipped dependencies are not leaked. Xcode should no longer need to evaluate deep nested include chains for transitive packages.

constraints.grounded: Do not emit standalone xcconfig files for dependencies that are only transitive. Do not include skipped, build-context, or non-visible dependencies. Do not inline unrelated components that are not reachable through declared CppInfo requirements or through the default public direct host dependencies of a non-component package. Preserve deterministic first-seen ordering while removing duplicated merged CppInfo values.
constraints.conceptual: Keep generated Xcode configuration complete for compilation and linking, but flatten the dependency structure and avoid introducing settings from dependencies the consumer did not actually require.

behavior: XcodeDeps collects a flat transitive CppInfo set for each generated direct dependency root package or component before rendering its conditional props.
Internal component requirements are traversed recursively within the same package and inlined into the requiring component's props.
External package/component requirements are resolved through the visible host and test dependency graph and recursively inlined.

For componentized external packages, a whole-package requirement inlines all sorted components, while a component-specific requirement inlines only the named component and its transitive requirements.
For packages without components and without explicit CppInfo requirements, direct host dependencies are treated as required transitive metadata and inlined recursively.
The same CppInfo reached through multiple dependency paths is included once, preserving first-seen ordering of merged values.
Generated package/component entrypoint xcconfigs no longer contain inter-package transitive dependency include directives; transitive metadata is placed in the conditional props files instead.

Only direct, non-build, non-skipped dependencies cause package/component xcconfig files to be generated; dependencies that are present only transitively no longer receive separate generated xcconfig files.
acceptance_criteria: Given a direct dependency with a deep transitive package/component graph, when XcodeDeps generates files, then the direct dependency's conditional props should contain the required transitive include directories, libraries, frameworks, defines, and flags without requiring nested inter-package includes.

Given a component that requires another component in the same package, when XcodeDeps generates that component's props, then the props should include metadata from both the component and its required internal component chain.

Given a component that requires an external package component, when XcodeDeps generates the requiring component's props, then the props should include that external component and its transitive requirements, and should not include unrelated components from the external package.
Given a requirement on an entire componentized external package, when XcodeDeps generates props for the requiring package or component, then all components of the external package should be inlined.

Given a package without components and without explicit CppInfo requirements, when it has direct host dependencies, then XcodeDeps should inline those direct host dependencies' required metadata recursively.
Given a dependency that is only transitive from the consumer's perspective, when XcodeDeps generates files, then it should not emit standalone xcconfig outputs for that transitive-only dependency.
Given a skipped or non-visible dependency in a transitive path, when XcodeDeps resolves transitive metadata, then that dependency should not be generated or inlined.

Given a diamond dependency graph where the same required component is reached through multiple paths, when XcodeDeps generates props, then the required metadata should appear without duplicate merged values and should exclude components that are not reachable from any declared requirement.

task_27.title: Retire CMake interface link directory property
task_27.description: Conan 2.28.0 removes support for the deprecated cmake_set_interface_link_directories property in CMakeDeps and CMakeConfigDeps generation. The generators should no longer inspect this property, emit property-specific deprecation warnings, or alter generated CMake target configuration based on it. Packages should rely on supported package metadata to describe link information.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the deprecated CMake interface link directory opt-in is fully retired from generated CMake dependency files, so recipes that still declare it no longer receive legacy handling and supported package metadata remains the source of link information.

expectation.grounded: CMakeDeps and CMakeConfigDeps must stop consuming the deprecated cmake_set_interface_link_directories package property from cpp_info. Setting this property must not emit property-specific deprecated warnings, must not be type-validated by these generators, and must not cause generated CMake target configuration content to add interface link directory behavior, including the former Windows-only behavior. Existing dependency target names, component mappings, configuration handling, and link library propagation must continue unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: The old CMake link-directory compatibility flag should be treated as removed. Users should see normal CMake dependency generation without legacy warnings or hidden output changes from that flag, and packages should express required link behavior through supported metadata.

constraints.grounded: Do not change CMakeDeps or CMakeConfigDeps behavior for packages that do not set cmake_set_interface_link_directories. Do not alter normal generation of dependency targets, component targets, configuration-specific target data, or system link libraries. The presence or value of the removed property must not affect generated output or diagnostics.
constraints.conceptual: Keep ordinary CMake dependency generation stable and limit the behavioral change to retiring the deprecated flag.

behavior: CMakeDeps no longer queries, validates, warns about, or interprets cmake_set_interface_link_directories.
CMakeConfigDeps no longer queries, validates, warns about, or interprets cmake_set_interface_link_directories.
Setting cmake_set_interface_link_directories to true no longer enables additional interface link directory content in generated CMake target configuration, including on Windows.
Setting cmake_set_interface_link_directories to false or to any other value has the same generator-visible effect as omitting the property.
Generated target configuration still preserves package target names, dependency target references, component mappings, configuration naming, and normal link library information.
acceptance_criteria: When a package recipe declares cmake_set_interface_link_directories and CMakeDeps is used, generation should complete without a warning caused by that property and without output changes attributable to interface link directory auto-linking.
When a package recipe declares cmake_set_interface_link_directories and CMakeConfigDeps is used, generation should complete without a deprecated or invalid-property warning caused by that property.
When the target operating system is Windows and the removed property is enabled, generated CMake target configuration should not add interface link directory behavior because of that property.

When the removed property is absent, CMakeDeps and CMakeConfigDeps output should remain consistent with prior normal behavior for targets, components, configurations, dependencies, and system link libraries.
When the removed property has a value these generators would previously have type-checked, the generators should ignore it rather than producing property-specific validation behavior.

task_46.title: Respect unset PowerShell virtualenv configuration
task_46.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes handling of explicitly unset configuration values so disabling the PowerShell virtual environment setting no longer causes PowerShell activation scripts to be produced. Unset configuration values should resolve to their defaults before type validation or conversion, and PowerShell virtual environment generation should be driven by explicit string command values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that explicitly unsetting the PowerShell virtual environment configuration disables PowerShell script generation instead of being interpreted as a usable PowerShell setting.

expectation.grounded: When `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` is explicitly unset with `!`, `Conf.get` should treat the stored unset value as absent and return the requested default before applying choice checks or type conversion. Calls that read `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` as a string should therefore receive no truthy value for an unset configuration, preventing `.ps1` virtual environment and VCVars script generation. Command wrapping should still use `powershell.exe` as the default PowerShell executable when a PowerShell launcher must be invoked and no explicit command string is configured.
expectation.conceptual: Disabling the PowerShell environment integration should behave as a real opt-out: no PowerShell activation artifacts should appear just because the setting was unset, while normal defaults should continue to apply where PowerShell execution is actually needed.

constraints.grounded: Do not treat an unset configuration value as the string form of `None`, do not raise choice or type errors for an explicitly unset value that has a default, and do not generate `.ps1` environment scripts unless `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` resolves to a non-empty string command. Preserve support for explicit PowerShell command strings such as `powershell.exe` or `pwsh`, including additional arguments, and preserve the default `powershell.exe` command for wrapping existing PowerShell launchers.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must only change the disabled-setting behavior and must not break existing explicit PowerShell configurations or the default command used when PowerShell launchers are intentionally present.

behavior: An explicitly unset configuration value is resolved to the caller-provided default before choice validation or string conversion.
Reading `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` with string type checking returns the default for an unset value instead of a truthy string representation of the unset state.
Virtual environment script generation does not add `.ps1` output solely because `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` was unset.
VCVars environment generation does not add PowerShell companion scripts solely because `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` was unset.
Wrapping a command with existing PowerShell environment launchers continues to default to `powershell.exe` when no explicit PowerShell command string is configured.
Explicit non-empty string values for `tools.env.virtualenv:powershell` continue to enable PowerShell script behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given the PowerShell virtual environment configuration is explicitly unset, when environment files are generated, then no PowerShell `.ps1` activation or environment launcher files should be created because of that setting.

Given the PowerShell virtual environment configuration is explicitly unset, when VCVars environment support is generated, then no PowerShell VCVars companion script should be created because of that setting.
When an unset configuration value is retrieved with a default and string type checking, it should return the default rather than a stringified unset value.
When an unset configuration value is retrieved with configured choices, it should not be rejected merely because it is unset if a default can be returned.
Given an explicit PowerShell command string is configured, when environment generation runs, then PowerShell script behavior should remain enabled.
Given PowerShell launcher files already need to be wrapped and no explicit command string is configured, when command wrapping runs, then it should invoke the default PowerShell executable.

task_36.title: Default download retry wait
task_36.description: Conan 2.28.0 changes the default wait between remote package download retries from immediate retry to one second, and makes retry-related configuration defaults visible in configuration listings. This improves retry behavior for transient download failures and makes the retry policy easier for users to discover.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan package downloads no longer retry immediately by default after a failed remote download, and ensure that retry configuration defaults are visible to users inspecting Conan configuration options.

expectation.grounded: When `core.download:retry_wait` is not configured, Conan's remote download retry behavior should use an integer default of 1 second between retry attempts. `conan config list` should expose `core.upload:retry` as default 1, `core.upload:retry_wait` as default 5 seconds, `core.download:retry` as default 2, `core.download:retry_wait` as default 1 second, `tools.files.download:retry` as default 2, and `tools.files.download:retry_wait` as default 5 seconds; it should also expose `core:policies` as a built-in configuration entry.
expectation.conceptual: Failed remote package downloads should pause briefly before retrying by default, while users can discover the default retry counts and wait times from Conan's configuration listing.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the configured override semantics for `core.download:retry_wait`; explicit integer values must continue to take precedence over the default. Preserve `core.download:retry` at default 2, `core.upload:retry` at default 1, `tools.files.download:retry` at default 2, and preserve the existing 5-second wait defaults for upload retries and generic file download retries.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only alter the default delay for remote package download retries and improve configuration discoverability; existing user overrides and other retry defaults should remain stable.

behavior: Unset `core.download:retry_wait` now resolves to 1 second instead of 0 seconds for Conan remote package download retry handling.
Explicit `core.download:retry_wait` values continue to control the number of seconds waited between remote package download retry attempts.

Built-in configuration descriptions now include types and default values for core upload retry count, core upload retry wait, core download retry count, core download retry wait, generic file download retry count, and generic file download retry wait.
The configuration metadata distinguishes the 1-second default for remote package download retry wait from the 5-second defaults used by upload retry wait and generic file download retry wait.
The built-in configuration list includes `core:policies`, and the `tools.cmake:configure_args` description is normalized without changing CMake behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given no `core.download:retry_wait` is configured, when a remote package file download fails and Conan performs a retry, then the wait between retry attempts should default to one second.
Given an explicit integer value for `core.download:retry_wait`, when a remote package download is retried, then Conan should use that configured wait value instead of the one-second default.
When users inspect Conan's built-in configuration list, it should show the default retry counts and retry wait values for core upload, core download, and generic file download settings.
When users compare retry defaults, `core.download:retry_wait` should be presented as one second while upload retry wait and generic file download retry wait remain five seconds.
When no retry count override is configured, the default retry counts should remain unchanged for core downloads, core uploads, and generic file downloads.

task_2.title: Allow patch-ng 1.19 dependency
task_2.description: Conan 2.28.0 expands its supported patch-ng dependency range so environments may resolve and use patch-ng 1.19.x, incorporating upstream patch handling fixes while preserving compatibility with previously supported 1.18.x releases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan can be installed and used with patch-ng 1.19.x so users receive upstream patch-ng fixes without losing compatibility with the existing supported 1.18.x dependency line.

expectation.grounded: The declared patch-ng runtime dependency for Conan must accept version 1.19.x in addition to the existing lower bound of 1.18.0, while still excluding patch-ng 1.20 and newer. Patch application behavior exposed through Conan should remain equivalent for patches that worked with patch-ng 1.18.0.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to upgrade dependency resolution to the latest supported patch-ng 1.19 release and continue applying recipe patches as before, with the benefit of upstream fixes and no observable behavior regression for existing valid patch workflows.

constraints.grounded: Do not drop support for patch-ng 1.18.x, do not allow patch-ng 1.20 or later, and do not change Conan's public patching APIs or expected patch results solely because the dependency range now includes 1.19.x.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be a compatibility expansion, not a behavioral redesign: existing installations and patch workflows should continue to work, while environments that choose patch-ng 1.19.x should be accepted.

behavior: Dependency resolution for Conan accepts patch-ng versions from 1.18.0 up to, but not including, 1.20.
Environments that previously failed dependency resolution only because patch-ng 1.19.x was outside Conan's allowed range are now valid.
Existing environments pinned to compatible patch-ng 1.18.x versions remain valid.
Conan's patch application behavior should remain observably unchanged for patch sets that already worked with patch-ng 1.18.0.
patch-ng 1.20 and later remain outside the supported dependency range.
acceptance_criteria: When installing Conan 2.28.0 in an environment that resolves patch-ng 1.19.x, it should accept that dependency version.
When installing Conan 2.28.0 in an environment pinned to patch-ng 1.18.x, it should remain compatible.
When dependency resolution proposes patch-ng 1.20 or newer, Conan's declared dependency constraints should not accept it.
When applying patches through Conan that succeeded with patch-ng 1.18.0, the same patch workflows should continue to produce equivalent patched sources with patch-ng 1.19.x.

task_4.title: Support insecure config package installs
task_4.description: Conan configuration package installation now supports explicitly disabling SSL certificate verification when fetching configuration packages from a provided repository URL, including per-URL control in conanconfig.yml. The behavior remains secure by default unless the user opts out through the new command-line flag or the configuration file URL metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can install Conan configuration packages from HTTPS repositories that require insecure SSL handling, while keeping SSL verification enabled by default and requiring the insecure opt-out to be explicit.

expectation.grounded: The `conan config install-pkg` command must accept an `--insecure` option that disables SSL verification only for the temporary remote created from `--url`. If `--insecure` is provided without `--url`, the command must raise a ConanException because conanconfig.yml-driven installs must express insecure URL behavior inside the configuration file. The conanconfig.yml `urls` section must continue accepting plain string URL entries as secure-by-default entries and must also accept mapping entries with `url` and optional `verify_ssl`, defaulting `verify_ssl` to true when omitted. Remotes created from conanconfig.yml URLs must preserve each entry's SSL verification value when resolving and fetching requested configuration packages.
expectation.conceptual: Configuration package installation should allow an explicit insecure connection mode for repositories whose SSL certificates cannot be verified, but it should never silently weaken security. Command-line installs may opt out only when the repository URL is supplied on the command line, while configuration-file installs must define the SSL policy alongside each URL in the file.

constraints.grounded: Existing `conan config install-pkg` behavior without `--insecure` must keep `Remote.verify_ssl` enabled. Existing conanconfig.yml files with string-only `urls` entries must remain valid and secure by default. Dictionary-style URL entries without `verify_ssl` must also remain secure by default. The insecure command-line flag must not globally affect configured remotes or conanconfig.yml URL entries.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve backward compatibility and secure defaults. Disabling SSL verification must be scoped to the specific repository source where the user explicitly requested it, and it must not change unrelated remotes or package installation behavior.

behavior: `conan config install-pkg <reference> --url <repo-url> --insecure` creates the temporary configuration install remote with SSL verification disabled.
`conan config install-pkg <reference> --url <repo-url>` continues creating the temporary configuration install remote with SSL verification enabled.
Using `--insecure` without `--url` causes the command to fail with a ConanException instead of applying insecure behavior implicitly.
When loading conanconfig.yml, each plain string entry in `urls` is interpreted as a URL with SSL verification enabled.
When loading conanconfig.yml, each mapping entry in `urls` uses its `url` value and honors `verify_ssl` when provided.
When a conanconfig.yml URL mapping omits `verify_ssl`, SSL verification remains enabled for that URL.
Configuration package graph resolution and fetching use the remotes built with the effective per-URL SSL verification settings.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package reference and a repository URL, when the user runs `conan config install-pkg` with `--url` and `--insecure`, it should fetch the configuration package through a temporary remote that does not verify SSL certificates.

Given a package reference and a repository URL, when the user runs `conan config install-pkg` with `--url` and without `--insecure`, it should fetch through a temporary remote that verifies SSL certificates.
When the user supplies `--insecure` without supplying `--url`, the command should fail and indicate that the insecure option is only valid with command-line URL installs.
Given a conanconfig.yml file with string URL entries, when configuration packages are installed from it, those URLs should be treated as SSL-verifying remotes.
Given a conanconfig.yml file with URL mapping entries, when `verify_ssl` is false for an entry, that specific URL should be used without SSL verification.
Given a conanconfig.yml file with URL mapping entries that omit `verify_ssl`, those entries should continue to verify SSL certificates.
Given multiple conanconfig.yml URL entries with mixed SSL settings, each generated temporary remote should preserve its own effective SSL verification behavior.

task_35.title: Deduplicate finalize folder output
task_35.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes duplicate console reporting around recipe finalization so the finalized output folder is reported only when a recipe's finalize() hook is actually executed. This reduces redundant installer output without changing finalization behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan reports a recipe's finalized output folder only once when finalize() is involved, avoiding duplicate finalized-folder notifications when the same finalized package is encountered more than once.

expectation.grounded: During binary installation, the finalized-folder success notification should be emitted only for a conanfile whose finalize() method is executed in that finalization flow. If a package or graph occurrence does not run finalize(), it should not produce an additional finalized-folder success notification. The notification should still identify the finalized output folder for the conanfile that was actually finalized.
expectation.conceptual: Users should see one finalized-folder report for each actual package finalization, with no repeated folder lines caused by repeated graph references or already-handled finalization.

constraints.grounded: Do not change whether finalize() is called, the finalized folder selected for a conanfile, recipe-side output produced by finalize(), artifact generation, graph processing, or other installer behavior. The behavioral change is limited to suppressing finalized-folder success notifications when finalize() did not run for that occurrence.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove redundant status output while preserving package finalization semantics and all non-duplicate user-visible behavior.

behavior: A conanfile that executes finalize() still produces a success notification for its finalized output folder.
A finalized-folder success notification is no longer emitted from finalization processing unless the corresponding finalize() call is executed.
When the same finalizable package is reached more than once during installation, repeated graph occurrences that do not run finalize() no longer print duplicate finalized-folder notifications.
The actual finalize() invocation, finalization side effects, and finalized folder value remain unchanged; only the redundant installer output is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package recipe whose finalize() hook runs during installation, when finalization completes, then Conan should print one success notification identifying that recipe's finalized output folder.
Given the same finalizable package is encountered multiple times in an install graph, when only one actual finalization occurs, then the finalized output folder should be reported only once.

Given an install graph occurrence for which finalize() is not executed because finalization has already been handled, when the installer processes that occurrence, then it should not emit another finalized-folder success notification.
When duplicate finalized-folder reporting is eliminated, package contents, generated artifacts, recipe finalization side effects, and other installer output should remain unchanged.

task_44.title: Validate Config Packages in Lockfiles
task_44.description: Conan 2.28.0 adds validation for lockfiles that record config_requires so commands using those lockfiles fail when the currently installed configuration packages are missing, extra, or incompatible with the locked configuration requirements. This prevents lockfile-based operations from silently running with configuration state that is not represented by the lockfile.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lockfile-based Conan operations reject configuration-package drift when a lockfile contains config_requires, instead of proceeding with installed configuration packages that are not aligned with the lockfile.

expectation.grounded: When a loaded Lockfile contains config_requires, ConanAPI.lockfile.check_lockfile_config must compare those locked configuration package references with the currently installed configuration package references. The operation must raise ConanException if any installed configuration package is not represented by the lockfile, or if the lockfile contains a config_requires package name for which no acceptable installed reference exists. Partial locked references, such as references without recipe revisions, must still be able to accept matching installed references.
expectation.conceptual: A Conan command that relies on a lockfile with configuration package requirements should only proceed when the user's installed configuration packages satisfy the lockfile. If the local configuration state is missing a required package or contains a conflicting package, the command should fail clearly before continuing.

constraints.grounded: Validation must be skipped when no lockfile is loaded or when the loaded lockfile has no config_requires entries. A lockfile may contain multiple config_requires references for the same package name; installing any one matching reference for that package name is sufficient. Existing lockfile behavior for package graph requirements, profiles, remotes, and lockfile resolution must remain unchanged apart from this config_requires alignment check.
constraints.conceptual: Projects without locked configuration packages should continue to work as before. The new validation should enforce reproducibility for locked configuration packages without making unrelated lockfile workflows stricter.

behavior: A lockfile-level validation now examines the lockfile's config_requires entries before continuing with supported lockfile-consuming commands.
If the lockfile has no config_requires entries, the validation is a no-op even when installed configuration packages exist.
If the current installation contains a configuration package reference that is not covered by the lockfile's config_requires, the command raises ConanException.
If the lockfile contains config_requires and none of the acceptable references for a required configuration package name are installed, the command raises ConanException.
If the lockfile records multiple acceptable references for the same configuration package name, one installed matching reference satisfies that package-name requirement.
A lockfile reference that does not pin a recipe revision can still match an installed configuration package reference that includes a compatible revision.
The alignment check is invoked for lockfile-aware install, build, create, export package, test, audit scan, graph, lock, and workspace command flows that load a lockfile.
acceptance_criteria: Given a command loads no lockfile, when it runs with installed configuration packages, then it should proceed without performing config_requires alignment validation.
Given a command loads a lockfile without config_requires, when installed configuration packages are present, then it should proceed as in the previous release.
Given a command loads a lockfile with config_requires and the installed configuration packages exactly match the locked references, then it should proceed.
Given a command loads a lockfile with a partial config_requires reference and the installed configuration package matches that reference with an additional recipe revision, then it should proceed.
Given a command loads a lockfile with config_requires and an installed configuration package is absent from the lockfile, then it should fail before continuing the requested operation.
Given a command loads a lockfile with config_requires and no installed package satisfies a locked configuration package name, then it should fail before continuing the requested operation.

Given a lockfile contains multiple config_requires references for the same package name, when one matching reference for that name is installed, then that package-name requirement should be treated as satisfied.

task_47.title: Honor transitive libs in CMakeConfigDeps for shared libraries
task_47.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps dependency propagation so requirements declared with transitive_libs=True continue to contribute their link libraries even when the relevant packages are shared libraries. This prevents generated CMake targets from omitting required transitive link dependencies while preserving existing exclusions for application targets and configured CMake target metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps honors transitive_libs=True for shared-library dependency chains so consumers receive the required transitive link libraries instead of losing them when intermediate dependencies are shared libraries.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps generates target dependency information, the link decision for a transitive package requirement must follow the corresponding requirement's libs trait, including requirements created with transitive_libs=True. This applies to global package targets and cross-package component requirements, including PackageType.SHARED dependencies. Same-package component requirements should remain public link dependencies. PackageType.APP dependencies and executable components should not be emitted as link libraries, and cmake_target_name and cmake_link_feature customizations should continue to be reflected in generated targets.
expectation.conceptual: A package that intentionally exposes another package's libraries to its consumers should have that relationship represented in generated CMake targets regardless of whether the packages are built as shared libraries. Non-library dependencies should remain excluded from link interfaces, and existing CMake naming and link-feature customization should keep working.

constraints.grounded: Do not suppress a transitive link solely because both the requiring package and required package are PackageType.SHARED when the requirement's libs trait indicates the dependency should be linked. Do not add APP packages or executable components to link interfaces. Do not discard component-level target names or link features configured through CMakeConfigDeps properties.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only restore intended library propagation and must not broaden link interfaces to non-library artifacts or ignore existing user-provided CMake target configuration.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now treats the requirement's libs trait as the observable source of truth for whether a transitive package target is linked.
Requirements declared with transitive_libs=True can propagate their library target through generated CMake dependencies even when the requiring package and required package are shared libraries.
Component requirements within the same package are represented as public link dependencies in generated CMake target information.

Cross-package component requirements can be linked when the corresponding requirement exposes libraries, while existing behavior for library components without an explicit requirement-level libs signal is preserved.
Application packages and executable components continue to be skipped as link-library dependencies.
Configured CMake target names and link features continue to apply to the generated dependency targets.
acceptance_criteria: Given a shared library package that requires another shared library with transitive_libs=True, when a consumer uses CMakeConfigDeps and links the intermediate package target, then the downstream library target should be present in the generated link interface.

Given the same dependency relationship for non-shared library builds, when CMakeConfigDeps generates targets, then the transitive library propagation should remain consistent with the requirement's libs trait.
When a dependency in the graph is an application package or executable component, it should not be emitted as a link-library dependency.
When a package component depends on another component from the same package, the generated component target should expose that dependency as a public link relationship.
When custom CMake target names or link features are configured for dependencies or components, those customizations should still be observable in the generated CMake dependency targets.

task_31.title: Preserve error-like option names in conan list
task_31.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes a display bug in the conan list command where option names containing the word error were incorrectly rendered as error entries. The command should now preserve such option names and values as normal listed data, while continuing to mark real error fields as errors.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that conan list preserves user-defined option names containing the word error and displays them as normal option data instead of converting them into error entries.

expectation.grounded: When conan list serializes and prints package or recipe data, keys whose names merely contain error, such as option names, must retain their original key name and associated value. Only keys whose normalized name is exactly error or pkgsign_error should receive error-style treatment. Existing warning handling for a normalized warning key should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Listing package data should distinguish real error indicators from ordinary user-defined names. A user option should not be reported as an error just because its name includes the word error.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable behavior of conan list for actual error fields named error or pkgsign_error, and do not change the existing handling of warning fields. Non-error fields must not be renamed or highlighted as errors solely because error appears as a substring.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be limited to correcting false error classification without weakening real error reporting or changing unrelated list output semantics.

behavior: conan list no longer treats every output key containing error as an error field.
User-defined options with names that include error are displayed using their original option name and value.
Fields named error continue to be displayed as errors.
Fields named pkgsign_error continue to be displayed as errors.
Fields named warning continue to keep their warning-specific display behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package with a user-defined option whose name contains error, when the package is listed with conan list, then the option name and selected value should appear as normal option data.
When conan list encounters an output field whose normalized key is exactly error, it should still present that field as an error.
When conan list encounters an output field whose normalized key is exactly pkgsign_error, it should still present that field as an error.
When conan list encounters an ordinary field or option name where error is only part of a longer name, it should not rename or format that field as an error.
When conan list encounters a warning field, its warning behavior should remain unchanged.

task_26.title: Remove Deprecated PackagesList Helpers
task_26.description: Conan 2.28.0 removes deprecated, non-public helper methods from PackagesList that previously only warned and delegated to supported APIs. Consumers must use the supported single-reference mutation APIs, revision-aware iteration, or serialization access patterns instead. The PackagesList.items() contract is also clarified to emphasize that it only yields artifact references when recipe revisions, and package revisions for packages, are present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that deprecated, non-public PackagesList helper methods are no longer available, and that users interact with package lists through the supported APIs for adding references, iterating revision-backed entries, and reading serialized list data.

expectation.grounded: PackagesList must expose add_ref(), add_pref(), items(), serialize(), recipe_dict(), package_dict(), and pref_dict() behavior while removing the deprecated add_refs(), add_prefs(), add_configurations(), refs(), and prefs() helpers. Accessing or calling the removed helpers should fail as unavailable attributes instead of issuing deprecation warnings or delegating to replacement methods. PackagesList.items() should yield RecipeReference values with dictionaries keyed by PkgReference only for data that includes recipe revision entries, and package entries should appear only when package revisions are present; callers that need raw search results without revisions should use serialize().
expectation.conceptual: Deprecated package-list shortcuts are removed from the usable API. Users should add package-list entries through the supported single-entry methods, iterate only fully revision-backed artifacts through items(), and use serialization when they need the raw list structure or broad search results that do not include revisions.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve compatibility shims, deprecation warnings, or bulk wrapper behavior for PackagesList.add_refs(), PackagesList.add_prefs(), PackagesList.add_configurations(), PackagesList.refs(), or PackagesList.prefs(). Do not change the supported add_ref(), add_pref(), serialize(), recipe_dict(), package_dict(), pref_dict(), or revision-filtering semantics of items().
constraints.conceptual: Removing the deprecated shortcuts must not alter the supported package-list operations or make broad serialized results inaccessible. Existing supported APIs should continue to represent recipe and package revisions consistently.

behavior: PackagesList no longer provides the deprecated bulk reference addition helper that accepted multiple recipe references and delegated to add_ref().
PackagesList no longer provides the deprecated bulk package-reference addition helper that accepted multiple package references and delegated to add_pref().
PackagesList no longer provides the deprecated configuration injection helper that attached package information only to already-present package IDs.
PackagesList no longer provides the deprecated refs() iterator-style helper that returned recipe revisions as a dictionary.
PackagesList no longer provides the deprecated prefs() helper for extracting package revision references from a recipe bundle.
Code that attempts to use any removed PackagesList helper observes normal missing-attribute behavior instead of a deprecation warning.
PackagesList.items() remains the supported revision-aware iterator and yields only entries backed by recipe revisions, with package references included only when package revisions exist.
PackagesList.serialize() remains the supported way to inspect the full stored list data, including results from searches that did not request revisions.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer inspects PackagesList, the deprecated helpers add_refs(), add_prefs(), add_configurations(), refs(), and prefs() should not be available.
When a consumer tries to call any removed PackagesList helper, it should fail because the attribute is absent rather than producing a deprecation warning or delegating to another method.
When a consumer adds a recipe reference through add_ref(), the package list should record the recipe revision data as before.
When a consumer adds a package reference through add_pref(), the package list should record the package revision data and optional package information as before.
When a package list contains recipe revisions, items() should yield recipe references and their associated package-reference data.
When a package list does not contain recipe revision data, items() should not yield artifact references for those entries.
When a consumer needs to read package-list data that may not contain revisions, serialize() should still return the stored structure for inspection.

task_38.title: Make recipe reference resolution case-sensitive
task_38.description: Conan 2.28.0 fixes a dependency resolution issue where recipe searches used for version ranges could match package references despite casing differences. Wrong-cased requirements should no longer silently resolve to recipes with different casing; they should remain unresolved so users see the casing error.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan treats package reference casing as significant during requirement resolution, especially when resolving version ranges, so a requirement with incorrect package-name casing does not match an existing recipe with different casing.
