expectation.grounded: Requirements declared through Conan recipe APIs such as requires with a package name whose casing differs from the available recipe reference must not be satisfied by case-insensitive recipe search. Version range requirements, including wildcard-style ranges, should only resolve against recipe references whose package-name casing matches the requested reference. If no correctly cased recipe satisfies the requirement, Conan should report the package as unresolved.
expectation.conceptual: Dependency resolution must respect the exact spelling of package names. A package name that differs only by uppercase or lowercase letters is a different reference for resolution purposes and must not be accepted as a match.

constraints.grounded: Recipe pattern searches must preserve case-sensitive matching semantics and must not reintroduce an ignore-case path for resolving package references. Correctly cased requirements and unfiltered recipe listings must continue to behave normally.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should prevent false positive matches caused by casing mistakes without changing successful resolution for correctly spelled package references or broadening the set of acceptable package names.

behavior: Recipe search patterns are evaluated case-sensitively instead of matching references regardless of case.
Version range resolution no longer selects a cached recipe whose package name differs only by letter casing from the requested requirement.
A wrong-cased requirement remains unresolved when no recipe with matching casing exists.
Correctly cased requirements continue to resolve against matching recipes.
Listing recipes without a search pattern remains unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: Given a cached recipe named with one casing, when a consumer requires the same package name with different casing and a version range, then dependency resolution should not select the cached recipe.
When a wrong-cased version range requirement has no exactly cased matching recipe, it should fail as an unresolved package instead of resolving to a differently cased recipe.
When the requirement uses the exact package-name casing of an available recipe and the version range is otherwise satisfiable, it should resolve successfully.
When recipe references are searched with a pattern, only references matching the pattern's casing should be included.
When recipes are listed without a search pattern, the full recipe list should still be returned.

task_29.title: Warn when remote auth ignores environment credentials
task_29.description: Conan 2.28.0 makes remote authentication more transparent when a remote accepts anonymous access. If credential environment variables are set but authentication is not forced, the command should warn that those variables were not used and direct users to force authentication when they intend to log in.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan remote auth` warns users when credential environment variables are set but the remote accepts anonymous access, causing those credentials to be ignored.

expectation.grounded: When `RemotesAPI` authenticates a remote without `force`, and credential validation leaves no authenticated user for that remote, it must inspect the relevant Conan credential environment variables with values: `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME_<REMOTE>`, `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME`, `CONAN_PASSWORD_<REMOTE>`, and `CONAN_PASSWORD`, where the remote-specific suffix uses the remote name uppercased with hyphens converted to underscores. If any such variables are present, Conan must emit a warning that identifies the remote, lists the ignored variables, and indicates that `--force` can be used to force authentication.
expectation.conceptual: When a remote allows anonymous access and Conan therefore does not consume configured credentials, users should receive a clear warning instead of having their login-related environment variables silently ignored. The warning should make it apparent which credentials were ignored and how to request authentication explicitly.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the successful anonymous access outcome: when anonymous access is accepted and `--force` is not provided, no user should be returned or persisted solely because environment variables exist. Do not emit the ignored-credentials warning when `--force` is provided, when an authenticated user is obtained, or when none of the relevant credential environment variables have values. Preserve the existing behavior for remotes that require authentication.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve visibility without forcing login, breaking anonymous access, or adding noise when no credentials were supplied. Users who explicitly force authentication should continue through the existing authenticated flow without receiving an ignored-credentials warning.

behavior: After a non-forced remote authentication attempt succeeds anonymously and no user is available for the remote, Conan checks for populated generic and remote-specific credential environment variables.

If one or more relevant credential environment variables are populated in that anonymous-access case, Conan emits a warning that the variables were ignored because the remote accepted anonymous access.
The warning includes the matching credential variable names so users can identify which configuration was bypassed.
The warning directs users to use `--force` when they want Conan to authenticate even though anonymous access is available.
When `--force` is used, the new warning path is skipped and the existing forced authentication behavior is preserved.
When no relevant credential environment variables are populated, anonymous access remains silent as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given a remote that accepts anonymous access and populated `CONAN_LOGIN_USERNAME` or `CONAN_PASSWORD` variables, when `conan remote auth <remote>` runs without `--force`, it should complete with anonymous access and emit an ignored-credentials warning.

Given populated remote-specific credential variables for a remote name, when anonymous access is accepted without `--force`, the warning should identify those remote-specific variables using Conan's normalized remote-name environment variable convention.

Given a remote that accepts anonymous access and no relevant credential environment variables, when `conan remote auth <remote>` runs without `--force`, it should not emit an ignored-credentials warning.

Given populated credential environment variables, when `conan remote auth <remote> --force` is used, Conan should attempt forced authentication through the existing credential flow and should not warn that those environment variables were ignored.

Given a remote that requires authentication, when credentials are supplied through the supported environment variables, the existing authentication behavior should continue without being treated as anonymous credential ignoring.

task_25.title: Remove Deprecated Deploy Folder Fallback
task_25.description: Conan 2.28.0 removes the deprecated Conan home deployer-extension folder compatibility behavior. Cache deployers should now be resolved from the current deployers cache folder only, without falling back to the old deploy folder or warning about that deprecated fallback.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan no longer supports the deprecated deployer extension folder named deploy in Conan home, and instead consistently uses the current deployers folder for cache deployers.

expectation.grounded: The Conan home deployer path resolution exposed by HomePaths.deployers_path should always resolve to the extensions folder named deployers. It should not return the deprecated folder named deploy when that folder exists, and it should not emit the previous deprecation warning associated with using that old folder.
expectation.conceptual: Users who provide deployer extensions through Conan home must use the current deployers location. The legacy deploy location is no longer treated as a supported compatibility alias.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the canonical deployers folder name or the behavior for deployers already available from the current deployers location. Do not preserve any fallback, discovery behavior, or deprecation warning that makes the old deploy folder function as a cache deployer source.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should remove only the deprecated compatibility path while keeping normal deployer discovery through the supported location intact.

behavior: The deployer cache path is resolved to the current deployers folder regardless of whether a deprecated deploy folder exists in Conan home.
A deprecated deploy folder in Conan home is no longer selected as the deployer extension source.
The previous warning tied to falling back to the deprecated deploy folder is no longer emitted because the fallback is removed.
Existing deployers stored in the supported deployers folder remain discoverable through the normal cache deployer lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Given Conan home contains deployer extensions in the supported deployers folder, when cache deployer lookup is performed, it should resolve deployers from that supported folder.
Given Conan home contains only the deprecated deploy folder, when cache deployer lookup is performed, it should not resolve that folder as the cache deployer source.
Given both the deprecated deploy folder and the supported deployers folder exist, when cache deployer lookup is performed, it should use the supported deployers folder.
When the deprecated deploy folder exists, cache deployer lookup should not emit a deprecated-folder compatibility warning or otherwise signal that the old folder is still being used.

task_40.title: Add short aliases for lock upgrade update options
task_40.description: The library update adds missing short command-line aliases to `conan lock upgrade` for the existing requirement update options, improving CLI consistency without changing the underlying lock upgrade behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan lock upgrade` supports concise short options for updating normal requirements, build requirements, and Python requirements while preserving the existing long options.

expectation.grounded: `conan lock upgrade` must accept `-ur` as an alias for `--update-requires`, `-ubr` as an alias for `--update-build-requires`, and `-upr` as an alias for `--update-python-requires`. Each alias must accept the same values, support repeated occurrences, and produce the same observable lock upgrade behavior as its corresponding long option.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to use shorter option names when requesting dependency updates during a lockfile upgrade, with no behavioral difference from using the established long option names.

constraints.grounded: Existing `--update-requires`, `--update-build-requires`, and `--update-python-requires` invocations must remain valid and must continue to support multiple values. The addition of short aliases must not alter other `conan lock upgrade` arguments or the semantics of resolving and applying updated requirements.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be backward-compatible and limited to command-line option spelling; dependency selection and lockfile update results should remain consistent.

behavior: `conan lock upgrade` recognizes `-ur` and treats it as the existing normal-requirement update option.
`conan lock upgrade` recognizes `-ubr` and treats it as the existing build-requirement update option.
`conan lock upgrade` recognizes `-upr` and treats it as the existing Python-requirement update option.
Repeated uses of the new short options accumulate update requests in the same way as repeated uses of the corresponding long options.
Short and long forms for the same update category are equivalent from the user's perspective and feed the same lock upgrade behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan lock upgrade` is invoked with `-ur` and a requirement reference or pattern, it should update matching normal requirements as it would with `--update-requires`.
When `conan lock upgrade` is invoked with `-ubr` and a requirement reference or pattern, it should update matching build requirements as it would with `--update-build-requires`.
When `conan lock upgrade` is invoked with `-upr` and a requirement reference or pattern, it should update matching Python requirements as it would with `--update-python-requires`.
When any of the new short options are supplied multiple times, all supplied update requests should be honored.
When users continue using the existing long options, their commands should remain accepted and produce the same results as before.

task_43.title: Fix workspace lockfile handling
task_43.description: Workspace install and build commands now handle explicit and default workspace lockfiles consistently, including partial lockfile mode, and avoid accidental use of package-local lockfiles that can cause crashes or incorrect dependency resolution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan workspace install` and `conan workspace build` use workspace-level lockfile semantics consistently, do not crash when an explicit partial lockfile is provided, and do not accidentally consume lockfiles from individual workspace packages.

expectation.grounded: `conan workspace install` and `conan workspace build` must resolve `--lockfile` from the user-provided argument when present, otherwise from the default workspace-level lockfile when available, and must preserve `--lockfile-partial` behavior. Package-local lockfiles must be ignored for workspace-level operations. Lockfile configuration must be checked before executing the workspace graph operation. Workspace consumer ConanFile helpers, including helper-backed recipe methods such as `self.run`, must remain initialized, and editable package generator behavior must honor the graph node recipe folder and editable output folder metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Workspace install and build should be deterministic: they should use one intended workspace lockfile, support partial lockfile workflows without crashing, and remain unaffected by stale or unrelated lockfiles inside member packages.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public command names or lockfile option names. Do not allow package-local lockfiles to override an explicitly supplied lockfile or an automatically discovered workspace-level lockfile. Do not regress the ability to run workspace operations with no lockfile, with an explicit lockfile, with a default workspace lockfile, or with partial lockfile mode. Preserve helper availability for workspace consumer recipes and preserve editable package output-folder behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should make workspace lockfile behavior predictable while preserving existing supported workflows and avoiding unrelated changes to normal install or build behavior.

behavior: `conan workspace install` and `conan workspace build` no longer crash when invoked with both an explicit `--lockfile` value and `--lockfile-partial`.
Workspace lockfile lookup is performed at the workspace level, so automatic lockfile discovery is based on the workspace root rather than on individual package folders.
If a workspace-level lockfile is explicitly provided or discovered by default, that lockfile is consistently propagated through workspace package install/build operations.
If no workspace-level lockfile is selected, workspace package operations are explicitly run without falling back to package-local lockfiles.
An explicitly empty lockfile option disables workspace lockfile use and still prevents package-local lockfiles from being picked up implicitly.
Workspace consumer ConanFile instances retain the helper initialization needed by helper-backed recipe methods during workspace graph processing.
Editable package generation uses the recipe folder and editable output folder associated with the dependency graph node, so editable output placement remains consistent during install operations.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace, when `conan workspace install` or `conan workspace build` is run with an explicit lockfile and `--lockfile-partial`, then the command should complete using that lockfile in partial mode without crashing.
Given a workspace-level default lockfile and no explicit lockfile option, when workspace install or build runs, then the workspace-level lockfile should be used for the workspace operation.
Given package-local lockfiles inside workspace package folders and no selected workspace-level lockfile, when workspace install or build runs, then those package-local lockfiles should not be used.

Given both package-local lockfiles and an explicitly selected workspace-level lockfile, when workspace install or build runs, then the selected workspace-level lockfile should take precedence for all workspace package operations.
Given an explicitly empty lockfile option, when workspace install or build runs, then no lockfile should be used and package-local lockfiles should still be ignored.
Given a workspace consumer recipe that relies on Conan helper-backed methods, when workspace graph processing occurs, then those helper-backed methods should remain available.

Given an editable package with an editable output folder, when install generation runs for that editable package, then generated outputs should respect the editable output folder associated with the graph node.

task_7.title: Show transitive requires in graph info HTML
task_7.description: The HTML output generated by `conan graph info ... -f=html` now supports an interactive node-subgraph view for transitive requirements. When enabled, selecting a graph node highlights that node, its reachable dependency nodes, and the outgoing dependency edges between them, while preserving the existing graph data and respecting current visibility and package-collapsing options.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users viewing `conan graph info ... -f=html` output can inspect the transitive requirements of an individual package as an interactive node subgraph without changing the underlying dependency graph.

expectation.grounded: `conan graph info ... -f=html` should expose a subgraph/transitive-requires mode in the generated HTML. When that mode is active and a graph node is selected, the page should select the starting node, all dependency nodes reachable through its `dependencies` relationships, and the outgoing dependency edges from each visited node. The behavior should work when package nodes are collapsed by resolving dependencies to the corresponding collapsed node identity, and it should leave hidden nodes unselected when current graph filters remove them from the rendered network.
expectation.conceptual: The HTML graph viewer should let a user focus on one package and see the full set of packages it requires, including indirect requirements, as a highlighted subgraph. This should be a viewing aid only: it should not alter the graph contents or dependency relationships.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the dependency graph data produced by `conan graph info`; limit the change to generated HTML interactivity and presentation. Existing controls for hiding build or test nodes, collapsing packages, showing package type, and selecting packages or edges should continue to operate. Collapsed package identifiers must remain distinct from real graph node identifiers so selection and edge traversal do not collide.
constraints.conceptual: The new subgraph view must be additive and non-disruptive. Existing graph filters, collapsed views, node and edge selection, and informational display behavior should continue to work, and the visualization should not misrepresent hidden or collapsed packages.

behavior: The generated `conan graph info ... -f=html` page gains a user-toggleable subgraph mode for inspecting a selected node's transitive requirements.
When subgraph mode is active and a visible graph node is selected, the HTML viewer recursively follows that node's dependency relationships and selects all visible reachable dependency nodes.
The selection includes outgoing dependency edges from each visited node, avoiding unrelated incoming or reverse-connected edges.
If package collapsing is enabled, dependency traversal resolves each dependency to its collapsed package node using the same node-labeling rules as the rendered graph.
Nodes hidden by current rendering filters are skipped rather than being forced into the selection.

Collapsed package node bookkeeping is available to the subgraph-selection logic across redraws, and generated collapsed node identifiers are allocated beyond existing graph node identifiers to avoid conflicts.
The empty-selection information prompt in the HTML viewer is simplified while retaining the same purpose of guiding users to select a package or edge.
acceptance_criteria: Given an HTML graph generated with `conan graph info ... -f=html`, when subgraph mode is enabled and a package node is selected, it should highlight that package and every visible transitive dependency reachable from it.
Given a package with both direct and indirect requirements, when the package is selected in subgraph mode, the highlighted subgraph should include indirect requirements as well as direct ones.

Given a graph where a selected package is required by other packages, when subgraph mode is active, incoming consumer edges should not be highlighted unless they are also outgoing dependency edges within the selected package's dependency traversal.

Given package collapsing is enabled, when a node is selected in subgraph mode, the highlighted dependency subgraph should use the collapsed package nodes consistently instead of losing or duplicating dependencies.
Given build or test nodes are hidden by viewer controls, when subgraph mode computes a selection, hidden nodes should remain absent from the visible selection.
Given subgraph mode is disabled, when a user selects a node or edge, the viewer should preserve the normal graph selection and information-display behavior.
Given no node or edge is selected, the viewer should display a prompt instructing the user to select one package or edge for information.

task_8.title: Improve Conan HTML report inspection
task_8.description: Conan 2.28.0 enhances generated HTML report output for dependency and diff inspection. The graph info HTML view adds clearer controls and an interactive subgraph mode so users can focus on a selected package and its transitive dependencies. The release note also identifies HTML report diff improvements for file-extension filtering and aligned diff context display.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated HTML reports make dependency and diff inspection easier: graph info HTML output should let users focus on a selected package's transitive dependency subgraph in the browser, and report diff HTML output should support narrowing results by file extension while keeping diff context visually aligned.

expectation.grounded: `conan graph info ... -f=html` and `conan graph info ... --format=html` output must include a `Show subgraph` control in the graph controls area. When this mode is enabled and a graph node is selected, the page must select the chosen node, every reachable transitive dependency node that is currently visible in the graph, and the outgoing dependency edges that connect that traversal. The behavior must continue to work with package grouping, existing visibility toggles, package search and exclusion controls, and node or edge information display. Based on the release note, `conan report diff ... -f=html` output should also allow filtering by file extension and should render diff context lines aligned with diff lines.
expectation.conceptual: Users opening generated HTML reports should be able to narrow what they are looking at without changing the underlying report. In graph reports, selecting a package should be able to reveal the dependency subset it brings in. In diff reports, users should be able to focus on relevant file types and scan context consistently.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the dependency graph data, graph resolution semantics, or the set of packages and edges emitted by `conan graph info`; the enhancement is limited to generated HTML presentation and interaction. Existing controls for build requirements, test requirements, skipped or binary nodes, package grouping, package type display, search, exclusion, legend, errors, and node or edge details must remain usable. Subgraph selection must skip nodes that are hidden by the current graph view and must not select unrelated reverse or upstream edges.
constraints.conceptual: The report should remain a faithful view of the same data while adding better ways to inspect it. Existing report controls and information should keep working, and the focused subgraph view should not imply relationships that are not present in the graph.

behavior: The graph info HTML output adds a clearer two-column layout with a controls sidebar and a separate information panel.
A new `Show subgraph` checkbox toggles subgraph selection mode in the graph info HTML UI.

When subgraph mode is enabled and a node is selected, the HTML page traverses that node's dependencies and updates the graph selection to include the selected node, visible transitive dependency nodes, and outgoing dependency edges from each traversed node.
Subgraph selection respects grouped package display by resolving dependencies to the currently displayed grouped package node when package grouping is active.
Subgraph selection skips graph nodes that are not visible under the current filters or visibility settings.
Graph edge identifiers are generated so node and edge selection can remain reliable when subgraph mode selects both nodes and edges.
Existing graph controls are exposed under an expandable `Extra graph controls` section instead of a dedicated show-or-hide checkbox.
The information panel prompt now covers both package and edge selection and resets to that neutral prompt when nothing is selected.
acceptance_criteria: Given a generated `conan graph info ... -f=html` page, when the user enables `Show subgraph` and selects a package node, it should highlight that node, its visible transitive dependency nodes, and the dependency edges connecting the traversal.
When package grouping is enabled and `Show subgraph` is active, selecting a node should highlight the grouped dependency nodes that are visible in the graph.
When graph controls hide build requirements, test requirements, skipped or binary nodes, searched-out nodes, or excluded packages, subgraph selection should not select hidden nodes.
When `Show subgraph` is disabled, selecting nodes or edges should retain the normal detail-display behavior without expanding the selection to the dependency subgraph.
When no package or edge is selected in the graph info HTML page, the information panel should show a neutral prompt inviting the user to select one.
When viewing graph controls, advanced graph controls should be available from an expandable extra-controls area while the existing graph toggles remain usable.
Given `conan report diff ... -f=html` output, users should be able to filter the displayed diff by file extension.
When viewing `conan report diff ... -f=html` output, unchanged context lines should align visually with changed diff lines.

task_37.title: Use User Locale in HTML List Dates
task_37.description: The HTML output for the Conan list command no longer forces English date localization. Dates shown in generated HTML should use the viewer's/browser's default locale while preserving the existing timestamp content and time formatting behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dates rendered by `conan list ... -f=html` respect the user's locale instead of always appearing in an English locale format.

expectation.grounded: `conan list ... -f=html` should render timestamp fields in its generated HTML by delegating locale selection to the user's runtime environment. The existing displayed date/time components, timestamp interpretation, and 24-hour time behavior should remain otherwise unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: HTML list reports should feel localized to the person viewing them: date values should follow the user's environment locale while keeping the same information and level of detail as before.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to date localization behavior in HTML list output. It must not alter the package list data, non-date fields, badge rendering, table structure, timestamp source values, or other `conan list` output formats.
constraints.conceptual: Only the locale used to present dates should change; the report contents, available fields, and other formats should continue to behave as they did previously.

behavior: Timestamp dates in `conan list ... -f=html` are formatted using the user's default locale rather than a forced English locale.
The HTML output continues to convert stored timestamp values into rendered dates for display.
The rendered date still includes the same date and time granularity, including hours, minutes, and seconds.
The rendered time continues to use the existing 24-hour clock behavior.
Users viewing the same generated HTML in environments with different locale settings may see locale-appropriate date ordering and separators.
acceptance_criteria: Given `conan list ... -f=html` output containing timestamped package or revision information, when the HTML is viewed in a browser configured with the user's locale, it should display dates according to that locale.
When the viewer's locale is not English, the HTML list output should not force English date ordering or separators.
When the viewer's locale is English, the HTML list output should continue to display the same timestamp information with no loss of date or time detail.
When generating HTML list output, package list content, non-date metadata, badges, and table layout should remain unchanged apart from localized date presentation.
When using non-HTML `conan list` output formats, behavior should remain unaffected by this locale fix.
